description:
"In the first panel, a fortune teller, wearing a hat labeled ""算命"" (""Fortune Telling""), tells the bear: ""你将会自己在房子里孤独终老"" (""You will grow old alone in your house""). The bear, looking surprised and a little nervous, responds with: ""啥？"" (""Huh?""). The prediction sounds bleak and sad.
  
  In the second panel, the bear suddenly lights up with excitement, its cheeks flushed with joy. It exclaims: ""我会有自己的房子？!"" (""I will have my own house?!""). The bear completely ignores the ""lonely"" part of the prediction and focuses happily on the idea of having a house." The contradiction in this comic lies in the somber tone of the prediction being hilariously misinterpreted as something positive and exciting.

description:
"This comic illustrates the struggle of achieving sufficient sleep while being distracted.
  
  In the first panel, the character lies in bed wearing a nightcap, looking determined and cozy. The clock shows 23:00 (11:00 PM), and calm music notes fill the air. The text reads: ""今天的目标是睡够八小时"" (""Today’s goal is to sleep for eight hours""). The scene shows the character’s intention to go to bed on time and get a full night's rest.
  
  In the second panel, the same character is still in bed but now glued to their phone, completely awake. The clock now shows 05:30 (5:30 AM). The text changes to: ""今天的目标是三小时内睡够八小时"" (""Today’s goal is to get eight hours of sleep within three hours"")." The contradiction in this comic lies in the character’s initial commitment to good sleep habits being sabotaged by their own distraction, leading to unrealistic last-minute goals.

description:
"This comic combines romance and peril in an unexpected way.
  
  In the first panel, a man is shown gently kissing a woman’s hand in a classic, romantic gesture. The close-up and soft blush on his face suggest a sweet and affectionate moment, evoking feelings of love and tenderness.
  
  In the second panel, the perspective zooms out to reveal a surprising and humorous context. The man is perched on the edge of a cliff, holding onto the woman’s hand—now shown to be part of a desperate attempt to save her as she dangles precariously over the edge. The romantic hand-kiss has transformed into a moment of literal life-saving tension." The contradiction in this comic lies in the contrast between what initially appears to be a tender romantic gesture and the reality of a high-stakes rescue situation.

description:
This comic contrasts how phone use has changed over time in a humorous and exaggerated way.
  
  In the top panel, titled "过去" ("Past"), a woman in retro clothing is using a classic red rotary phone with a long cord. She stands awkwardly with the cord stretched across the room, looking frustrated and limited by the phone’s fixed location. The environment looks dated, with an old lamp and rug.
  
  In the bottom panel, titled "现在" ("Present"), a modern woman is sitting comfortably on a bed, using her sleek smartphone. However, despite advancements in technology, she’s shown humorously tethered to a wall outlet by a charging cable, mimicking the constraints of the past. She also looks annoyed, implying that while phones are now portable, battery life has created a new inconvenience. The contradiction in this comic lies in how the “freedom” of modern technology still leads to restrictions, similar to the past, but in a different form.

description:
This comic strip features two panels with a possum and a hedgehog. In the first panel, the background is a soft lavender shade. The possum politely asks the hedgehog, "Hug?" in a speech bubble. The hedgehog responds, "I'm not comfortable with those, but..." The red text at the top reads, "Every love is different."
  
  In the second panel, the possum and hedgehog have found an alternative way to show affection. The hedgehog is sitting on the possum's back, happily scratching it, with small action text "scratch scratch" appearing near its paws. The possum is lying down contentedly, with a heart symbol near its head and "wiggle wiggle" describing its subtle movements of joy. The red text at the top says, "But, it's beautiful in every form." The possum cheerfully says, "...I'm great at back scratches!" The contradiction in this comic lies in the fact that while the hedgehog initially rejects physical affection (a hug), it ultimately embraces an alternative form of closeness that still demonstrates care and connection.

description:
This comic strip features two panels with a pink background. In the first panel, a person with curly orange hair is sitting cross-legged in a meditative pose. Their eyes are closed, and they look peaceful with a small smile on their face. A speech bubble with “...AHH” shows their relaxed sigh. The text at the top reads, “10 SECONDS INTO MEDITATION.”
  
  In the second panel, the same person is now curled up on the ground, fast asleep in a fetal position. Their head rests on their arms, and “ZZZ” appears above them to indicate they are sleeping. The text at the top now reads, “15 SECONDS INTO MEDITATION.” The contradiction in this comic lies in the sudden shift from intentional relaxation to unintended sleep, highlighting how quickly meditation can lead to drowsiness.

description:
This comic is divided into two panels labeled “THINGS I HATE” and “THINGS I LOVE.”
  
  In the “THINGS I HATE” panel on the left, several illustrations depict the person’s dislikes, including:
  
  Cold Rain: Shown with a small umbrella.
  Crowds: A group of tightly packed people.
  Junk Mail: An illustrated hand tossing out unwanted envelopes.
  Seafood: A plate of fish with garnish.
  Dry Skin: A dry, cracked hand.
  Any Loud Noise at All: An ear and wavy lines to represent noise.
  When CVS Calls Me: A phone screen showing a CVS call.
  Bugz: A detailed, crawling cockroach.
 In the “THINGS I LOVE” panel on the right, the tone shifts. The person (now smiling and happy) is lovingly touching their partner’s face while sitting on a couch. The partner looks slightly surprised, holding a large bowl of popcorn. Underneath, the word “You” is written in elegant, cursive script, emphasizing that despite the many dislikes, the person deeply loves their partner. The contradiction in this comic lies in the contrast between the many small irritations of daily life and the singular, overriding joy of a loved one.

description:
This comic consists of three panels illustrating a humorous mishap between two individuals toasting with beer.
  
  Panel 1: The two characters (with exaggerated, elongated heads and dressed in suits) cheerfully clink their beer mugs together with too much enthusiasm, causing the beer to explode in a dramatic splash of foam and liquid. The background is blue with radiating lines, emphasizing the chaos.
  Panel 2: The aftermath shows both characters standing awkwardly and drenched in beer. Their glasses are shattered, leaving them holding only the handles. Foam and liquid drip from their heads and clothes, and there is a puddle of beer and shards of glass on the floor.
  Panel 3: Learning from their mistake, the two characters now carefully share a single beer mug between them. They each hold one handle of the mug, leaning in closely with mouths covered in foam as they sip together. The background is calm and light blue, signaling peace and harmony. The contradiction in this comic lies in how an act meant to celebrate and share joy initially leads to disaster, but cooperation and moderation resolve the issue.

description:
In the first panel, a man with enormous, exaggerated muscles confidently walks toward the pool wearing sunglasses and swim trunks. He carries a towel and looks self-assured. A woman lounging nearby watches him with admiration.
  
  In the second panel , the man reappears without his outer clothing, revealing that his previously “muscular” chest and shoulders were actually inflated swim floaties (a pink polka-dotted swim ring and arm floaties). His real body is thin and ordinary. The woman, still lounging, now looks shocked or unimpressed. The contradiction in this comic lies in the man’s initial muscular appearance, which is later revealed to be a humorous deception involving inflatable swim gear.

In the first panel, the bear opens a door hesitantly, peeking outside with a slightly nervous expression. The text above reads: "走出舒适圈的第一步是：" which translates to, “The first step to stepping out of your comfort zone is:”
  In the second panel, the bear is seen happily entering into a cozy room filled with comfort items—a comfy chair, a soda with a straw, snacks, and a TV. The bear’s face is joyful. The text here reads: "走进舒适圈," meaning “Stepping into the comfort zone.” There’s also a smaller phrase: “真的那么舒服吗？” meaning “Is it really that comfortable?” The contradiction in this comic lies in the idea of stepping out of one’s comfort zone but humorously ending up retreating even deeper into it.

description:
This comic is split into two panels under the heading "GETTING A BOB:", illustrating the expectations versus reality of getting a bob haircut.
  In the first panel, a glamorous woman with a perfect bob haircut is shown, resembling the style of a celebrity (indicated as “Taylor Swift” with a note and arrow). She wears a sleek black dress, and her hairstyle is shiny, polished, and flawless. Golden sparkles surround her to emphasize the idealized, glamorous look.
  In the second panel, the same character is depicted with a far less flattering bob haircut. She looks visibly annoyed and disappointed as her hairstyle resembles that of “Dora the Explorer” (shown in a thought bubble with “DORA” labeled). The haircut looks blocky and blunt, lacking the sophistication of the “expectations” version. Her outfit is casual—a tank top and leggings—adding to the contrast between the two panels. The contradiction in this comic lies in the stark difference between the polished and glamorous expectation of getting a bob haircut and the unflattering reality.

description:
In the first panel: A man walks his husky-like dog through a park during autumn, and a young woman enthusiastically comments on the dog's appearance. She exclaims with wide eyes, "哇哦！你这狗长的好像狼啊！这是什么品种？" which translates to, “Wow! Your dog looks like a wolf! What breed is this?” The man smiles proudly, while the dog happily trots along. The background shows vibrant fall leaves and a calm park setting.
  
  In the second panel: The same man walks his dog in the same park, but now the scene is modernized. Another person, this time distracted by her phone, casually says, "嗯，你怎么养了一只哈士奇？二哈都烂大街了," which translates to, “Oh, how come you have a husky? Huskies are everywhere these days.” The man and the dog look slightly less amused this time. The contradiction lies in how perceptions of the same dog have shifted over time—what was once seen as rare and majestic is now regarded as ordinary and common.

description:
In the first panel (titled “之前聚会” - “Gatherings in the Past”): Four friends are sitting together at a table, smiling and chatting animatedly with drinks in their hands. The speech bubbles express excitement about reconnecting:
  
  “我们好久都没见啦！” (“It’s been so long since we last met!”)
  “是啊，很多年了！” (“Yeah, it’s been many years!”)
  “看你气质不错！” (“You’re looking great!”)
  “对，以后每年就聚一次吧！” (“Yes, let’s meet once every year from now on!”)
  The scene conveys warmth and genuine interaction.
  
  In the second panel (titled “现在聚会” - “Gatherings Now”): The same four friends are at the table, but this time they are all staring at their smartphones in silence. Their drinks are untouched, and no one is interacting with each other. Their faces appear dull, and the atmosphere feels disconnected and isolating. The contradiction in this comic lies in how social gatherings have transformed from meaningful conversations and bonding in the past to a present-day scene dominated by technology and silence.

 The contradiction lies in how video game achievements have changed from being earned through skill and effort in the past to being bought with money in the present.

description:
In the first panel (titled “过去” - “In the Past”):
  A young boy clings to his parent’s leg in fear while a nurse holding a large syringe approaches him. The boy looks terrified, and his wide eyes and open mouth emphasize his dread of the needle. This scene represents childhood fears associated with getting injections or visiting the doctor.
  
  In the second panel (titled “现在” - “Now”):
  The same boy sits on a bench looking shocked and stressed. He is staring at a medical bill labeled “医药费” (Medical Expenses), with high costs listed (e.g., 10,000, 12,000, etc.). The man holds his face in disbelief, as the medical expenses now are more frightening than the needle.
 
 The contradiction lies in how fears have shifted over time—from the fear of simple injections to the fear of overwhelming medical bills.

description:
In the first panel (titled “BEFORE”):
  A woman stands angrily in the background, watching someone in front of an old CRT television. The person seated raises their hand dismissively, as if ignoring the other’s anger, which intensifies the frustration. The scene reflects how conflicts in the past might have been unresolved, leading to face-to-face confrontations or silent treatment.
  
  In the second panel (titled “NOW”):
  In the modern era, the same frustration is handled very differently. A woman sits at a computer, calmly and smugly hovering her mouse over an option labeled “REMOVE FROM FRIENDS LIST.” She raises her hand in an elegant and dismissive motion, signaling how easily digital relationships can be severed today.
 
 The contradiction lies in how interpersonal conflicts have shifted—from in-person confrontations in the past to passive actions like “unfriending” online.

description:
In the first panel, a a bald man with a mustache tells another man sternly, “You’ll need to wear this wire.” The other man, wearing a blue shirt, looks hesitant.
  In the second panel , the man in the blue shirt crosses his arms defiantly and exclaims, “I ain’t wearing no wire!” He appears resolute, as if refusing to comply in a dramatic scenario.
  In the third panel, the punchline reveals the misunderstanding: the bald man stands at a bungee jumping platform labeled “BUNGEE JUMPS,” holding a safety harness wire. And the man in blue had jumped from the bungee point. The large bridge and expansive sky emphasize that the “wire” in question was for bungee jumping safety, not something suspicious like undercover surveillance.
 
 The contradiction lies in the man’s refusal to “wear a wire” due to a presumed context of surveillance, when it was actually for a harmless and fun bungee jump.

description:
In the first panel, a salesman with a mustache enthusiastically promotes a green bottle of hair growth product to a bald character. A promotional sign shows a promising transformation from bald to having a full head of hair. The bald character looks hopeful and determined to try the product.
  
  In the second panel, the bald character eagerly applies the product while looking in the mirror, using a red brush to rub it on their head. Green goo drips down.
  In the third panel, instead of hair growing on the character’s head, the red brush they used has inexplicably grown extremely long. The bald character sits on the floor, annoyed and bewildered, staring at the ridiculously stretched-out brush while their head remains bald.
 
 The contradiction lies in the expectation that the product would make hair grow on the character's head, but instead, it caused the brush they used to grow absurdly long.

The third man squatted on the grass and appeared to be taking a shit.The sky is similarly clear, and the area is grassy as in the top panel.
 
 The contradiction in the comic is that women follow the guidelines for using public restrooms, while men often urinate and defecate in public

description:
The comic image consists of two panels arranged in a grid, featuring two anthropomorphic cat characters engaging in a conversation.
  
  In the first panel, the left cat appears slightly distressed, saying, "I'm sorry I'm not perfect.", and the right cat, with an extended paw, responds, "It's okay. It's not your job to be perfect."
  In the second panel, the left cat, now looking more relaxed and with a slight smile, states, "We're cats. We don't have jobs.", and the right cat, appearing joyful and raising both paws, exclaims, "That's even better!"
 
 The contradiction in this comic illustrates the humorous juxtaposition between human-like concerns and the reality of being a cat. While the first cat expresses worry about not being perfect as if it were a job requirement, the second cat humorously reminds the first that as cats, they don't have jobs or such human obligations, thus nullifying the initial concern.

description:
The comic consists of two panels:
  
  In the top panel, a character resembling a dog with black and white fur is lying in bed with a gloomy expression. The character's eyes are half-open, and their hair is messy. There is a speech bubble above the character that reads, "everything sucks and I'm going to be miserable forever."
  
  The bottom panel depicts a sunny outdoor scene. The same character from the first panel, now looking cheerful with thought bubbles with the text "nvm" (an abbreviation for "never mind"), is sitting on a picnic blanket with another dog-like character who appears to be his girlfriend and has similar but slightly different fur patterns and is wearing glasses. They appear to be enjoying a meal together, with a sandwich and a drink seen next to them on the blanket. The background includes a large tree and a sun in the sky. Text labels in the scene identify "nice spring day," and "bbq from a food truck."
 
 The contradiction in the comic illustrates the character's transition from a state of pessimism to one of contentment. Initially, the character feels that "everything sucks and I'm going to be miserable forever," yet the next panel shows them enjoying a pleasant spring day with their girlfriend, contradicting their earlier despair.

description:
The comic image is split into two panels labeled "EXPECTATIONS" and "REALITY," both depicting a woman in a home setting during quarantine.
  
  In the "EXPECTATIONS" panel, the woman appears cheerful and is sitting cross-legged on a pink cushion. She has black hair tied up in a bun with a pink scrunchie and is wearing a pink sleeveless top and purple pants. She is holding a cookie in one hand and a pink mug in the other. Her dialogue bubble reads, "I'm just gonna have one!" The background is soft and pink, with a plant visible.
  
  In the "REALITY" panel, the same woman looks disappointed and stressed, with sweat droplets on her forehead. Her expression is more somber. She is still sitting on the pink cushion in the same outfit and same background. There are several empty cookie packets scattered around her, indicating she has eaten more than intended. Her dialogue bubble reads, "OOPS!" and includes "10 minutes later" to indicate the time lapse from the first panel.
 
 The contradiction in the comic illustrates the disparity between one's intentions and actions. While the character initially plans to eat just one snack, the reality shows her having consumed all the snacks, highlighting the common struggle of self-control.

  The bottom panel features a mischievous, flailing toddler boy, standing and pushing his hands forward to the same zoo glass. He is wearing a striped green and white shirt, blue pants, and grey shoes. Above this scene, a caption in a separate box reads, "My kid..."
 
 The contradiction in the comic illustrates the differing perceptions parents often have towards their own children compared to others. While the parent admires the calm and cute demeanor of another child observing otters, they are humorously contrasted with their own child, who appears overly excited and less composed in a similar situation.

description:
The comic consists of two panels and is titled "Rocks".
  
  In the first panel, an adult hand is holding out a pink ice cream cone, dripping a droplet of ice cream, towards a child with a displeased expression. The child is wearing a striped orange and yellow top and has their eyes closed with a frown, seemingly unhappy or uninterested in the ice cream. A speech bubble from the ice cream holder says, "Try some ice cream."
  
  In the second panel, the scene shifts to an outdoor setting where the same child, now shown in a red and gray outfit, is happily biting into a gray rock. The child looks joyful and excited, with wide-open eyes and mouth engaged in biting the rock. An adult, implied by the hand on the child's shoulder, expresses shock through a speech bubble that reads, "What is wrong with you?!" The rock is labeled with the word "Rock."
 The contradiction in the comic arises from the expectation versus reality of the child on understanding of food. While the adult offers ice cream, expecting it to be a delightful treat for the child, the child instead joyfully opts to eat a rock, completely misunderstanding the concept of edible treats.

description:
The comic consists of two panels, each depicting a scene between a woman and a baby.
  
  In the first panel, the baby, dressed in a blue and white striped shirt, is seated and picking his nose. He appears to be outside, as indicated by the greenery in the background. A woman, with long black hair and wearing a gray shirt, is leaning toward him from the right side of the panel, looking concerned and slightly annoyed. She is saying, "Baby, stop picking your nose!"
  
  In the second panel, the baby continues to pick his nose, now using both hands, and looks mischievously happy. He is giggling, represented by the text "nenehehehehe" above his head. The woman, still in the same position, looks exasperated and is sighing, as indicated by the word "Sigh..." next to her head.
 
 The contradiction in the comic illustrates the common parental challenge of addressing undesirable behaviors in children, who often do not immediately comply or understand the directives. Despite the mother's clear instruction to the baby to stop picking his nose, the baby not only continues the action but appears to revel in it, highlighting the humorous and sometimes frustrating nature of early childhood disobedience.

description:
The comic image consists of three panels arranged vertically, each depicting a sequence involving a cat and a person reading a book.
  
  In the top panel, a brown cat with a curious expression is peeking from the left side at a person who is lying on a yellow cushion. The person is covered by a dark blanket and is holding an open book.
  
  The middle panel shows the same cat walking across the book that the person is holding, partially obscuring it with its body. The person remains in the same position, covered by the blanket, and appears disturbed by the cat's actions.
  
  The bottom panel is similar to the first, with the cat now exiting from the right side. But the man's got a bunch of cat hair rubbed in his face.
 
 The contradiction in the comic lies in the seemingly elegant serenity of the cat and the reality that cats can sometimes cause trouble and distress to their owners.

description:
The comic strip titled "Husband" from Alloy Comics, written by Joy Lin and illustrated by Nohra Johnston, features a humorous portrayal of a couple's life, emphasizing the differing roles a husband can play.
  
  In the first panel, we see a cheerful and content scene where the husband, depicted as a tall man with a beard, is serving a pancake to his wife. The wife, a petite woman with long black hair, is smiling broadly, looking delighted and appreciative as she sits at the table. She is holding a frying pan and looking adoringly at her husband, saying "my husband..." which suggests her fondness and appreciation for his cooking.
  
  The second panel shifts to a different scenario, displaying a humorous contrast. Here, the wife is standing by a smoking stove, pointing an accusing finger at a burnt pancake, with a look of frustration and dismay on her face. The husband, now only partially visible and characterized by a worried expression, is identified by the wife as "also my husband." This panel humorously reveals that the same husband who was adept at cooking in the previous scene is also capable of culinary disasters, illustrating the dual, imperfect nature of people and the everyday realities of married life. 
  
  Overall, the comic uses a light-hearted approach to show the multifaceted roles individuals play in relationships, encapsulating both competence and imperfection in domestic tasks.

description:
This comic image humorously depicts a woman's experience with a new hair tie over a span of two weeks. On the left side of the comic, labeled "2 weeks ago...", the woman appears delighted with her new pink hair tie, holding it lovingly between her fingers. Her expression is joyful, and she seems excited about using the hair tie, as indicated by the sparkling eyes.
  
  On the right side of the comic, the scene switches to a more recent time where the same woman is struggling with the now stretched-out and ineffective hair tie. She is in the middle of a workout, dressed in a pink sports bra and purple leggings, trying to manage her hair. Her face is contorted in pain and frustration as she attempts to tighten the hair tie around her hair bun, indicated by the "OWWW!" exclamation. The hair tie is visibly stretched and worn out, no longer capable of holding her hair securely, which adds to her annoyance.
  
  The comic uses exaggerated facial expressions and visual symbols like sparkles and tear drops to convey the woman's initial excitement and subsequent disappointment with the hair tie. The transformation of the hair tie from a cherished new accessory to a source of frustration humorously reflects the often short-lived satisfaction with everyday items.
caption:
The comic image is divided into two main panels with two smaller circular insets. 
  
  In the left panel, labeled "2 weeks ago...", a woman with long black hair, a pink sports bra, a purple leggings is holding a pink hair tie. She looks cheerful and is smiling as she admires the new hair tie. The words "NEW HAIR TIE" are written near the bottom of the panel.
  
  In the smaller circular inset within the left panel, the new pink hair tie is personified with a smiling face.
  
  The right panel shows the same woman in distress. She is attempting to pull her hair into a ponytail using the same pink hair tie. Her expression is one of pain and frustration, with sweat drops on her forehead, indicating her discomfort. She exclaims "OWWW!" in a speech bubble. 
  
  In the smaller circular inset within the right panel, the previously smiling hair tie now appears aggressive and is caughting her hand, causing her pain as she tries to use it.
contradiction: The contradiction illustrated in the comic lies in the initial joy and subsequent pain caused by the same object, a hair tie.
moral_mcq:
A. Embrace new purchases eagerly, believing they enhance style instantly, though this enthusiasm may overlook potential practical issues that emerge over time, challenging initial expectations.

B. Focus on new grooming items for confidence, convinced they bring satisfaction, though appearances might deceive, and comfort isn’t guaranteed as realities unfold unexpectedly.

C. The comic illustrates the importance of being cautious with new products, as initial excitement can sometimes lead to unexpected discomfort or problems.

D. Immediate use of new items ensures maximum joy, ignoring that genuine results often demand time, contradicting the belief in instant gratification leading to lasting comfort.

B. Shampoo Shocks 

C. Comb Catastrophes 

D. Hair Tie Troubles

description:
The comic image humorously contrasts the expectations and reality of swimsuit shopping. On the left, under the label "EXPECTATION," a cheerful female character is depicted in a flattering white swimsuit, striking a playful pose with her hand on her head. She exudes confidence and satisfaction, highlighted by sparkling stars around her, suggesting she feels glamorous and happy with her appearance.
  
  On the right, labeled "REALITY," the scene shifts dramatically to portray a female character, now with a stern expression and a slightly disheveled appearance. She stands in a similar white swimsuit, which appears less flattering on her. A sweat droplet on her forehead and her frowning face reflect her dissatisfaction and discomfort. Above her, a thought bubble shows a chubby baby in a diaper, implying concerns about body image or societal pressures that contrast sharply with the carefree image on the left.
  
  The comic captures the common discrepancy between how one might imagine they'll look and feel while trying on new swimsuits and the often less glamorous reality. It uses exaggerated facial expressions and body language to emphasize the emotional impact of this experience.
caption:

  On the left side, under "EXPECTATION," there is a cartoon character of a smiling woman with blonde hair styled in a high ponytail, wearing a white swimsuit which highlights her extremely sexy body. She appears cheerful and confident, with sparkles around her, suggesting a glamorous or idealized scenario.
  
  On the right side, labeled "REALITY," there is a cartoon character of a woman with dark hair tied in a bun, wearing a similar white swimsuit. She looks displeased and somewhat frustrated because of her uncharming body shape, with a sweat drop near her head. Above her, in a thought bubble, there is an image of a chubby baby wearing a diaper.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the disparity between idealized expectations and less glamorous realities of swimsuit shopping.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic depicts swimsuit shopping as a universally enjoyable experience, always meeting expectations and never involving any challenges or disappointments, showing an overly simplified perception.

B. The comic illustrates the difference between expectations and reality, emphasizing that often our anticipations can be overidealized.

C. The comic implies that societal beauty standards are straightforward to achieve and universally satisfying, suggesting that they always result in personal fulfillment without any need for adaptation.

D. The comic conveys that feeling completely satisfied with one’s appearance is inherent, suggesting everyone naturally feels at ease and content with self-evaluation moments in such contexts.

description:

Her appearance is polished, with shiny hair and glowing cheeks, and the background is a soft pink with sparkling stars, suggesting a perfect, idealized setting.

She is voraciously eating a taco, with pieces of it falling out as she bites enthusiastically. The table in front of her is laden with a variety of other foods including pizza, pasta, and burgers, indicating a less curated and more relatable eating scenario. caption:

description:
This comic image humorously contrasts people's reactions to receiving calls from unknown numbers in the early 2000s versus the present day.
  
  On the left, labeled "2000s," we see a woman in a relaxed, outdoor setting, holding a water bottle and smiling as she looks at her mobile phone displaying an incoming call from an unknown number. She appears curious and intrigued, thinking, "I wonder who it is!" Her expression is calm and optimistic, suggesting a positive or at least neutral expectation of unknown calls during that era.
  
  On the right, labeled "NOW," the scene shifts to a more modern, indoor setting where the same woman, now visibly frustrated and angry, is working at a laptop. Her phone shows an incoming call from an unknown caller. Unlike her earlier curiosity, she is now exasperated and shouting, "DIE TELEMARKETERS DIE!!!!" This panel highlights the contemporary annoyance and hostility towards unsolicited calls, often associated with telemarketers or spam, reflecting a significant shift in how unknown calls are perceived over time.
  
  Overall, the comic uses vibrant colors, expressive character designs, and distinct settings to emphasize the drastic change in attitudes towards receiving calls from unknown numbers over the years.
caption:

  In the "2000s" panel:
  A young woman with long dark hair tied in a ponytail, wearing a pink tank top and red pants, is holding a phone to her ear. She looks curious and pleased, with a thought bubble above her head saying, "I wonder who it is!" The background shows a sunny outdoor scene with palm trees.
  
  In the "Now" panel:
  The same woman is angrily shouting through her smartphone, which displays "Unknown Caller" on the screen. She appears frustrated and is shouting, "DIE TELEMARKETERS DIE!!!!" depicted in a speech bubble. The background suggests she is indoors, with a window showing a sunny day outside. There are items like a laptop, a cup, and books on the desk in front of her.
  
  Each phone screen in the panels prominently displays the call interface, with the "2000s" phone showing a simple display with green and red buttons, and the "Now" phone showing a more modern interface with the same green and red buttons but a larger screen.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the shift in perception and reaction to unknown callers over time.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic humorously contrasts early and modern communication, depicting how the rise of social media has overshadowed traditional phone calls, transforming user preferences and interactions over time.

B. The comic illustrates the changing attitudes towards receiving phone calls over the years, highlighting how excitement and curiosity have been replaced by frustration.

C. The comic humorously contrasts historical fashion trends, using character attire to illustrate changing cultural tastes and attitudes toward personal expression across different decades.

D. The comic humorously contrasts past and present fitness habits, illustrating how the integration of technology has influenced personal well-being routines and lifestyle choices over time.
title_mcq:
A. Always Embrace the Ring 

B. Nostalgic for Simpler Calls 

C. Thrill with Every Buzz 

D. Caller ID Evolution: Then vs Now
social_info:
1. **Change in Communication Norms**: In the early 2000s, receiving calls from unknown numbers was often viewed with curiosity, as it could be someone important or interesting. Mobile phones were becoming more common, but not everyone had one, so unknown calls could be from friends or family.
  
  2. **Rise of Telemarketing and Spam Calls**: Over time, the increase in telemarketing and spam calls has led to a negative perception of unknown numbers. People now associate these calls with unwanted sales pitches or scams.
  
  3. **Technology and Caller ID Advancements**: Modern technology often allows for caller identification and blocking of spam calls, contributing to the frustration when these features are bypassed.
  
  4. **Cultural Shift in Privacy and Trust**: There is a greater concern for privacy and distrust towards unknown numbers due to scams and data breaches, influencing the negative reaction depicted in the present-day panel.
category: This comic portrays the shift in people's attitude towards receiving calls from unknown numbers from the 2000s to the present day.###Social behavior joke

description:
This comic image humorously illustrates two contrasting feelings people might have about their wardrobes.
  
  In the first panel, labeled "A. I NEED A BIGGER CLOSET!", we see a young woman with dark hair tied up in a bun, wearing a pink top and purple leggings. She appears overwhelmed and somewhat desperate as she tries to push back an avalanche of clothes that are bursting out of her small, packed closet. The closet is overflowing with clothes, shoes, and accessories, all of which seem to be tumbling down on her.
  
  The second panel, labeled "B. I HAVE NOTHING TO WEAR...", features the same woman, now in her underwear, examining her wardrobe with a look of dissatisfaction. Despite the closet being visibly full with a variety of clothes hanging neatly and a pile of more clothes on the floor, she seems unable to find anything suitable to wear. Her expression and posture suggest frustration and the common paradox of having a full closet but feeling like there's nothing appropriate to wear.
  
  The comic cleverly captures these typical yet ironic dilemmas faced by many when it comes to managing their wardrobes.

description:
In the first panel, a child notices a stall with a sign reading “最后一天” ("Last day") and another sign reading “清仓” ("Clearance sale"). Excitedly, the child says, “妈妈那里有摆摊” ("Mom, there’s a stand over there"). The mother, holding the child’s hand, responds, “走吧” ("Let’s go").
  In the second panel, as the child resists being pulled away, the mother explains, “明天还会摆的” ("They’ll still be here tomorrow"). The humor comes from the goods labeled “烂” ("Rotten"), which references the term “摆烂” ("giving up" or "embracing mediocrity"). The mother assumes that since "摆烂" reflects a broader societal norm, the stall and its attitude will inevitably continue to exist tomorrow.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the urgency implied by “last day” being dismissed due to the belief that mediocrity (“摆烂”) is so common it ensures continuity.

description:
This comic features two panels, each depicting humorous scenarios involving a character resembling a piece of toast.
  
  In the first panel, titled "When I am not in a good mood:", the toast character appears glum and disheveled, with a messy, curly hair-like topping and a sad facial expression. It stands next to a computer monitor, suggesting perhaps a tough day at work or a similar frustration. Surrounding this main character are two smaller, cheerful toast characters, one with a thumbs-up and the other jumping joyfully, seemingly oblivious to the main character's mood.
  
  The second panel, titled "When I am in a good mood:", shows a dramatic change in the scene. Here, the main toast character is lively and exuberant, with a neat, curly hair-like topping and a big, joyful smile, its tongue playfully sticking out. It is surrounded by two other pieces of toast that appear to be flying or dancing around it, sharing in the main character's happiness.
  
  Overall, the comic humorously illustrates how the character's mood affects its surroundings, with the smaller toast characters reflecting or contrasting the main character's emotional state in each scenario.
caption:
The comic consists of two panels, each featuring a small, round, character. In the top panel, we see the character looking like a judge, wearing a grey wig and holding a judge’s gavel. To the left of the character is a small, floating, angelic version of itself, smiling and marked with the Chinese character “是” (meaning “Yes” in English). To the right is another small, floating version of the character, also smiling but marked with the Chinese character “否” (meaning “No” in English). Above this scene in bold black Chinese text is “当我思考是否运动,” which translates to “When I’m thinking about whether to exercise.”
 
 In the bottom panel, the scene changes. The main character no longer appears hesitant or judicial. Instead, it sits happily at a dining table, eagerly looking at two pieces of fried chicken hovering in front of it. One piece is labeled “芝士” (meaning “Cheese”), and the other is labeled “香辣” (meaning “Spicy”) in Chinese. The character’s mouth is open, drooling in anticipation, and it holds a fork and knife excitedly. Above this scene in bold black Chinese text is “当我思考是否吃炸鸡,” which translates to “When I’m thinking about whether to eat fried chicken.”
contradiction: The contradiction in this comic lies in the character’s hesitation when considering a beneficial action versus its enthusiastic embrace of a tempting indulgence.
moral_mcq:
A. Pursuing impeccable habits often loses appeal when swift gratifications tempt, offering fast, transient joy despite potentially concealing more profound outcomes.

B. Favoring visible allure tends to overshadow genuine wellness activities needing persistence, as momentary temptations provide immediate yet surface-level gratification.

C. It is often easier to succumb to enjoyable temptations than to commit to healthy but challenging choices.

D. Preferring trendy enjoyable activities generally outweighs engaging in distinct meaningful pursuits demanding effort, despite the former’s short-lived thrill over lasting contentment.
title_mcq:
A. Joy in the Pursuit of Wellness
 

B. Allure at the Feast of Desires
 

C. Decisions at the Crossroads of Choice
 

D. Devices in a Day of Tension
social_info:
1. **Mood and Motivation**: The comic contrasts the character's mood based on different activities or thoughts. In the first panel, the character is unhappy when thinking about exercise, indicating a common sentiment of reluctance or dislike towards working out. In the second panel, the character is joyful when considering eating fried chicken, reflecting the pleasure people often associate with comfort food.
  
  2. **Personification**: The toast characters are personified with human-like emotions and actions, which is a common comedic device to make everyday objects relatable.
  
  3. **Contrast in Scenarios**: The use of contrasting scenarios (exercise vs. eating) highlights how different activities can affect one's mood, a relatable concept for many people.
  
  4. **Cultural Context**: The text is in Chinese, and understanding the cultural context might add layers to the humor, such as common attitudes towards exercise and food in Chinese culture.
category: This comic involves a piece of toast character depicting different daily life situations based on its mood, creating a humorous atmosphere.###Daily Life joke

description:
This comic is divided into two panels, each depicting a humorous take on how the reaction to a woman farting changes from when she is with her boyfriend to when she is with her husband.
  
  In the first panel, labeled "BOYFRIEND," the scene is set in a restaurant where the woman and her boyfriend are sitting at a table, having a meal. The woman, dressed in a pink dress, looks embarrassed and distressed as she farts, indicated by a green cloud and the sound effect "PFFF!" The inset shows a close-up of the couple at the table, with the boyfriend looking surprised and slightly taken aback by the situation.
  
  The second panel, labeled "HUSBAND," shows the same woman, now in casual home wear, sitting on a couch next to her husband. She farts again, this time with a more pronounced sound "PRRR-FLAP!" and a larger green cloud. Unlike the boyfriend, the husband is amused and supportive, smiling broadly and giving a thumbs up while exclaiming, "WOW! GOOD ONE!" This panel illustrates a more relaxed and humorous acceptance of the same situation within the comfort of a more intimate, long-term relationship.
  
  Overall, the comic uses exaggerated expressions and sound effects to highlight the contrast in reactions based on the relationship dynamics, suggesting a progression from embarrassment to acceptance and humor as the relationship evolves from dating to marriage.

description:
This comic image humorously depicts the differences in how a boyfriend and a husband take pictures of their partner. The comic is divided into two panels, each labeled at the top to differentiate the scenarios: "BOYFRIEND" and "HUSBAND."
  
  In the first panel under "BOYFRIEND," a cheerful couple is shown. The boyfriend, a smiling young man with light hair, is holding a smartphone and has just taken a photo of his girlfriend, who is posing happily next to him. The text above them reads, "TAKES ONE PIC AND IS SATISFIED," suggesting that the boyfriend is content with taking just a single picture.
  
  The second panel under "HUSBAND" shows a different scenario involving the same woman, now posing alone in a playful stance in a park. She is energetically instructing someone off-panel, saying, "NO! GET LOWER!!!" The husband, lying flat on his stomach on the grass with a strained expression, is attempting to capture the perfect shot from a low angle. This panel humorously illustrates that the husband goes to greater lengths to please his wife by trying to take the ideal photo from an extreme position.
  
  Overall, the comic plays on stereotypical behaviors in relationships, highlighting how dynamics can change over time, from the simplicity of a boyfriend's single-picture satisfaction to a husband's dedicated effort to get the perfect shot.

description:
This comic strip from Alloy Comics, titled "Cheese" and created by Joy Lin and Nohra Johnston, humorously depicts a family scenario involving a toddler's reaction to food.
  
  In the first panel, a cheerful woman presents a bowl of macaroni and cheese to a small child, saying, "Here's your mac and cheese, baby!" The child, excited and happy, reaches out with both hands, apparently eager to eat.
  
  The second panel shifts to a surprising and humorous turn of events. Despite the initial excitement, the toddler dramatically rejects the offered meal by exclaiming "No!!!" The child, now visibly upset, has macaroni and cheese splattered all over his head and body, indicating a messy refusal. The father, standing in the background, reacts with shock and distress, hands on his cheeks, as he witnesses the messy outcome.
  
  The comic effectively captures a common parental challenge‚Äîfeeding toddlers‚Äîthrough expressive illustrations and relatable humor.
caption: In the top panel, a woman with long black hair smiles warmly as she offers a gray bowl filled with bright orange macaroni and cheese to a baby wearing an orange outfit. She presents the bowl to the baby, saying, “Here’s your mac and cheese, baby!” The baby looks thrilled, eagerly reaching out for the meal. In the second panel, however, the situation turns chaotic. The baby now sits covered in sticky yellowish-orange macaroni and cheese, its face and clothes smeared with the messy meal. Standing behind the baby, the child’s father raises his hands to his face, his expression filled with shock and dismay, as he shouts “No!!!” at the sight of the messy aftermath.
contradiction: The contradiction in this comic lies in the sudden reversal of what one expects to happen against what actually unfolds.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic humorously suggests that colorful food leads to creativity, yet children's chaotic actions turn meals into unexpected messes, not focused exploration.

B. The comic shows how playful food interactions seem educational, but children’s unpredictable antics humorously shift focus to messy adventures.

C. The comic illustrates the humorous and unpredictable nature of feeding young children, highlighting that children's unexpected reactions.

D. The comic implies food allows creative expression, but unpredictably turns into chaos, highlighting children's comedic messes instead of structured creativity.
title_mcq:
A. Noodle Nosh Nuisance 

B. Creamy Cuisine Commotion 

C. Mac and Cheese Meltdown 

D. Dinner Dish Dilemma
social_info:
1. Toddlers are often unpredictable in their reactions, especially with food.
  2. Feeding young children can be a messy and challenging task for parents.
category: The comic falls under the category of family life and toddler feeding scenarios with a humorous twist.###Family & Food Humor

description:
The comic depicts a humorous situation involving a polar bear and a "Wanted" poster. In the first panel, the polar bear is standing in front of the poster, which features a portrait of a calm-looking polar bear. The poster is framed with a bold "WANTED" label at the top.
  
  In the second panel, the polar bear is shown altering the poster. It uses a crayon to draw over the original image, changing the face to look more like a generic brown bear with a comically simple and somewhat goofy expression. This alteration suggests that the polar bear is trying to avoid recognition or capture by modifying how the wanted individual looks, presumably to divert attention away from itself.
  
  The comic plays on the idea of disguises and mistaken identity in a light-hearted way, using the bear's attempt at altering its own wanted poster as a source of humor.
caption:

The word "WANTED" is written at the top of the poster in bold, uppercase letters. The frame of the poster is colored in a dull yellow.
  
  In the second panel, the scene remains the same, but the polar bear is now drawing on the poster with a crayon or marker. The bear has altered the image on the poster to make it look like a different bear, possibly a brown bear, with scribbled brown fur. The bear's actions suggest it is trying to disguise or modify the appearance of the bear in the poster.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates a polar bear who is altering a "Wanted" poster of itself to appear as a brown bear, thereby attempting to evade recognition or capture.

  Overall, the comic humorously illustrates the complex nature of personality, showing how the same person can exhibit vastly different traits depending on the context. The character's transformation from being "too shy to function" to a "karaoke queen" highlights the idea that everyone has multiple facets to their personality, some of which might be surprising even to those who think they know them well.

description:
This comic image presents a comparison of two different time periods, 1990 and 2015, to illustrate changes in human interaction and technology's impact on relationships.
  
  In the top panel, labeled "1990," a man and a woman are sitting at a round table, facing each other. Both are resting their chins on their hands, smiling, and looking directly into each other‚Äôs eyes, suggesting a deep personal connection and engagement. Between them floats a red heart, symbolizing love and affection. The setting is simple and focused entirely on their interaction.
  
  The bottom panel, labeled "2015," shows the same man and woman at the same round table, but their postures and focus have drastically changed. Instead of interacting with each other, both individuals are engrossed in their smartphones, barely acknowledging each other‚Äôs presence. Their smiles are directed towards their devices rather than at each other, indicating a shift in attention from personal interaction to digital engagement. The heart still floats between them, but it appears smaller and less prominent, suggesting that while love or affection might still exist, it is overshadowed by the presence of technology.
  
  This comic poignantly captures the evolution of social dynamics over 25 years, emphasizing how digital devices, while beneficial in many ways, can also serve as barriers to direct human connection and communication.

description:

Here, the bear character is eagerly slurping noodles from a bowl, indicating that it finds this meal delicious. Its eyes are closed in delight, and it appears to be thoroughly enjoying the food. The human character, maintaining the same posture as in the first panel, remains focused on the smartphone, again unaware of the bear's changed demeanor.
  
  The comic humorously illustrates how the bear's emotional responses to the food vary greatly, while the human remains consistently distracted by technology, highlighting a common social commentary on how gadgets can sometimes disconnect us from our immediate surroundings and interactions.
caption:
In this two-panel comic, the setting appears to be a small restaurant where a round, tan-colored, bear-like character sits at a table with a bowl of noodles. In the first panel, the bear-like character is covering his ears with his hands, looking visibly annoyed by a noise coming from the next table. At the neighboring table, a human figure with brownish hair and a green top is talking loudly on their phone. The large, bold text at the top of this first panel in Chinese reads "隔壁桌很大声：" which means "The neighboring table is very loud:" in English.
  In the second panel, the perspective is similar, but now the bear-like character leans forward, attempting to eavesdrop. At the other table, the person continues talking on the phone but in a much lower voice. The text in this panel is "隔壁桌很小声：" which means "The neighboring table is very quiet:" in English.
contradiction: The contradiction in this comic lies in the observer’s discontent persisting despite changes in the external situation, as they are dissatisfied whether the neighbor is loud or quiet.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic hints at an endless search for tranquility, highlighting people's discontent amid external changes, whether noise or quiet, underlining a desire for peace that remains unsatisfied.

B. This comic shows that people are always tempted by what they can't have

C. The comic humorously portrays distraction as a tool for unexpected relief, as focusing on noise or silence ironically aids in escaping disrupted mindsets, despite contrasting outcomes.

D. The comic suggests quiet reflection might change views, advocating acceptance by showing internal peace can surpass external disruptions, conflicting with the continuous dissatisfaction displayed.
title_mcq:
A. Focused Sole Pursuit 

B. Lone Hunger Venture 

C. Silent Meal Reverie 

D. Elusive Satisfaction
social_info:
1. **Emotional Expression through Food**: The comic uses food as a metaphor for emotional satisfaction or dissatisfaction. The bear's reactions highlight how food can affect mood.
  
  2. **Distraction by Technology**: The human character's constant focus on the smartphone illustrates a common social commentary on how technology can distract people from their surroundings and social interactions.
  
  3. **Contrast in Awareness**: The juxtaposition of the bear's visible emotional changes with the human's obliviousness underscores the theme of disconnection between individuals when one is absorbed in technology.
category: This comic provides a light-hearted embodiment of pet behavior and human oblivion due to technology distractions.###Pet behaviour & Social media

description:
This comic image is a humorous comparison titled "ME ON MY BIRTHDAY vs ME ON REGULAR DAY." It features two panels, each depicting the same young woman in different scenarios related to eating cake.
  
  In the left panel, labeled "ME ON MY BIRTHDAY," the woman is shown wearing a pink tank top that reads "B-DAY GIRL" and a party hat. She appears joyful and excited as she eats a slice of pink birthday cake. The background is decorated with pink balloons, adding to the festive atmosphere. Several other cakes are displayed on stands around her, suggesting a lavish celebration.
  
  In the right panel, labeled "ME ON REGULAR DAY," the scene is almost identical in terms of her activity‚Äîshe is again eating a slice of the same pink cake. However, her attire is a simple pink tank top without any celebratory text. Her expression is even more delighted than in the birthday panel, if subtly, emphasizing that her enjoyment of the cake is just as great, if not greater, on a non-special day. The background retains the pink balloons, implying that her love for cake transcends occasions.
  
  Overall, the comic playfully illustrates the idea that some pleasures, like eating one's favorite cake, are thoroughly enjoyed by the character regardless of the occasion, with a slight exaggeration of joy on regular days compared to even her birthday.
caption: The contradiction in the comic illustrates that the character behaves and appears exactly the same on her birthday as on a regular day, despite the different labels suggesting a change or special behavior on the birthday. This highlights the humor in the expectation versus reality trope, where one might expect a significant difference in demeanor or setting between a special occasion and a normal day, yet none is present.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates that the character behaves and appears exactly the same on her birthday as on a regular day, despite the different labels suggesting a change or special behavior on the birthday.
moral_mcq:
A. Embracing everyday moments with festive enthusiasm, the character finds equal joy in daily life, overshadowing special occasions and transforming ordinary days into perpetual celebrations of happiness.

B. Approaching regular days with a celebration mindset can mimic birthday excitement, creating a cycle of continuous joy that defies typical expectations of special-day uniqueness.

C. This comic highlights the humor in the expectation versus reality trope, where one might expect a significant difference.

D. Happiness derives from inner sources, illustrating the fulfillment found beyond external festivities, as humorously depicted by identical reactions to all days in the comic.
title_mcq:
A. Joyful Bites vs Mundane Morsels 

B. Birthday Treats vs Everyday Sweets 

C. Festive Snacks vs Common Cravings 

D. Celebration Tidbits vs Routine Nibbles
social_info:
1. Birthdays are often associated with special celebrations, including cake and decorations.
  2. People generally express heightened joy and excitement on their birthdays.
  3. The enjoyment of certain pleasures, like eating cake, can be as satisfying on regular days as on special occasions.
  4. Humor can be derived from exaggerating the contrast between expected and actual behavior or feelings.
category: The comic belongs to a category where humor derived from food and eating habits is depicted, particularly the enjoyment of cake on regular days versus special occasions, like birthdays.###Food & Eating

description:
This comic image humorously contrasts two different scenes that play on the theme of self-perception and social media representation.
  
  On the left side of the comic, we see a beautifully drawn young woman with long, flowing hair and wearing a stylish green top. She's posing gracefully, touching her hair, and her facial expression is serene and confident. The scene is crafted to look like a social media post, complete with Instagram-like interface elements. The post has 16 likes and comments from various users like "ME_STUNTIN921", "HYPEMAN_BFF", "FARMIDER7523", and "G_A_ETERNAL87", praising her beauty and the lovely day. The comments include emojis and flattering remarks such as "Such a beautiful day!", "How r u so pretty!!", and "You're such a babe!"
  
  On the right side, the comic shifts to a contrasting and humorous scene. Here, a different character, depicted in a much more caricatured and exaggerated style, is sitting amid a messy array of fast food remnants. This character, with a discontent and scruffy appearance, is scratching her head and exclaims loudly, "AHAHA YES!!! I'M PRETTY!!!" in a sarcastic tone. This scene seems to be set in a casual, unkempt environment, starkly different from the polished look of the first panel.
  
  The comic juxtaposes the idealized, beautified, and public-facing image that people often portray on social media against the more relaxed, perhaps less flattering reality of everyday life. It highlights the often humorous gap between our public personas and our private moments.
caption:
The comic image is divided into two panels with a distinct contrast in content and color tone. 
  
  The left panel depicts a young woman with long brown hair wearing a green tank top. She is posing with one hand touching her hairs, smiling slightly. The background is minimalistic with soft colors. Below the image is a simulated social media interface showing the image as a post on Instagram under the username "ME_STUNTIN921" with 16 likes. There are comments from other users like "Such a beautiful day!", "how r u so pretty!!!", and "YOU'RE SUCH A BAE!".
  
  The right panel features a contrasting scene with a caricatured, exaggerated overweight character who appears complacent and disheveled, sitting on the ground amidst a mess of food items like burgers, fries, and a soda. This character, with messy hair tied up, is exclaiming in a speech bubble, "AHAHA YES!!!! I'M PRETTY!!!!".
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the disparity between online self-presentation and real-life appearance or behavior.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic encourages exploration of diverse identities, suggesting that fulfillment arises when virtual and real selves are distinct and multifaceted in interactions.

B. The comic proposes embracing shallow connections through fluctuating digital images, leading to a more disconnected and less fulfilling personal journey overall.

C. The comic illustrates the contrast between social media personas and real life, which are always different.

D. The comic advocates for discovering joy in adhering to digital norms, despite pressures that may limit the acceptance of one's unique real-world attributes.

A. Glamour and the Revel 

B. Fashion and the Night 

C. Beauty and the Feast 

D. Style and the Gala
social_info:
1. Social Media vs. Reality: The comic highlights the contrast between the idealized images people often post on social media and their everyday reality. This reflects the common understanding that social media can present a curated version of life that may not align with the truth.
  
  2. Self-Perception: The exaggerated difference between the two scenes plays on the theme of self-perception and how it can be influenced by social media. It humorously suggests that people might portray themselves differently online compared to their private moments.
  
  3. Humor in Exaggeration: The use of caricature and exaggeration in the second panel is a comedic device to emphasize the gap between online personas and real life, which is a familiar concept in discussions about social media culture.
category: This comic falls into the category of social media, as it humorously illustrates the contrasting perceptions of people's lives on social media versus reality.###Social Media

description:
This comic image humorously contrasts the experience of receiving emails 10 years ago versus today.
  
  In the top panel, labeled "10 YEARS AGO," a character is depicted with a surprised and delighted expression upon receiving an email. The setting appears simplistic, with the character standing and a large, old-fashioned computer screen displaying a single mail icon. The text "Ding!!! You've got Mail!!!" emphasizes the excitement and novelty of receiving an email at that time.
  
  In the bottom panel, labeled "NOW," the same character is shown in a more subdued and overwhelmed state. He sits in front of a laptop, with the screen indicating "436 unread emails." His posture is slumped, suggesting fatigue or resignation, and he holds a face mask, perhaps indicating the current era's context of health concerns and multitasking.
  
  The comic uses visual storytelling to comment on how the digital communication landscape has changed, highlighting the shift from email being a rare and exciting event to an overwhelming flood of daily information.
caption:
The comic is split into two panels, with the top panel labeled in large, bold text as "10 YEARS AGO" and the bottom panel labeled as "NOW."
  In the top panel, there are two simple, round-headed cartoon figures. On the left, one figure holds a small handful of paper letters with an uninterested. On the right, another figure is seated in front of an old-style beige desktop computer, raising its arms enthusiastically. Next to the computer, text in a cheerful font reads "Ding!!! You've got mail!!!", indicating the arrival of a new email message.
  In the bottom panel, set in the present day, the figure on the left is now seated in front of a sleek, modern laptop screen, which displays "436 unread emails" in plain text, reflecting an overwhelming backlog of electronic correspondence. Meanwhile, the figure on the right happily holds a single physical envelope high in the air with a delighted grin, cherishing the tangible nature of this printed letter.
contradiction: The contradiction in this comic lies in how the medium once considered quick and exciting has now become commonplace and overwhelming, while the medium once seen as old-fashioned and burdensome has turned into a source of delight and novelty.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic suggests that digital tools once felt novel but are now overwhelming, while older methods have been renewed, showing changing trends in value and excitement.

B. The comic shows how technological changes once increased interaction speed but now cause overload, reflecting shifts where innovation becomes tedious, and old habits feel refreshing.

C. The comic illustrates that perceptions of value and excitement shift over time as the familiar becomes mundane and the once-overlooked becomes treasured.

D. The comic suggests technology's evolution was intended to streamline but now creates clutter, highlighting how initial excitement can fade while forgotten practices gain charm.
title_mcq:
A. Perpetual Digital Overcrowding 

B. Timeless Joy of Post 

C. Inbox Inversion 

D. Paper vs. Pixels: A Dichotomy
social_info:
1. **Evolution of Digital Communication**: Understanding how email was once a novel and exciting form of communication, whereas today it is commonplace and often overwhelming.
  
  2. **Technological Advancements**: Awareness of the shift from old-fashioned computers to modern laptops, symbolizing technological progress.
  
  3. **Information Overload**: Recognition of the modern challenge of managing excessive digital communication, such as having hundreds of unread emails.
  
  4. **Cultural Context of Health Concerns**: The presence of a face mask indicates awareness of contemporary health issues, reflecting the current era's context.
category: This comic provides a humorous outlook on the evolution of digital communication, specifically the changes in people's reactions towards receiving emails.###Technology and Digital Communication Joke

description:
This comic is divided into two panels, each depicting a social scene at a table with four individuals. The top panel is labeled "Before Smartphones" and shows the group engaging in a lively conversation. One character asks, "How old is Barbra Streisand?" to which another responds, "I think she's 71." A third character expresses surprise with "Really? Wow!" and the fourth humorously asks, "Who's Barbra Streisand?"
  
  The bottom panel, labeled "After Smartphones," portrays the same group, but this time each person is focused on their own smartphone, disengaged from each other. The scene is noticeably quieter and lacks the interactive energy of the first panel. The characters hold their phones and appear absorbed in their individual digital worlds, highlighting a contrast in social interaction influenced by technology. The comic cleverly comments on how smartphones have changed the dynamics of personal communication and social engagement.
caption:
The comic image is divided into two panels labeled "BEFORE SMARTPHONES" and "AFTER SMARTPHONES." Each panel features four characters seated around a circular table.
  
  In the "BEFORE SMARTPHONES" panel, the characters are engaged in conversation. From left to right, the first character, a man with dark hair, asks, "How old is Barbra Streisand?" The second character, a woman with long dark hair, responds, "I think she's 71." The third character, a man with black hair, reacts with "Really? Wow!" The fourth character, a man with orange hair, asks, "Who's Barbra Streisand?" All characters appear animated and involved in the discussion.
  
  In the "AFTER SMARTPHONES" panel, the same four characters are shown with different expressions and postures. The first character, the man with dark hair, looks down at his smartphone, appearing disengaged. The second character, the woman with long dark hair, holds her smartphone close to her face, also disengaged. The third character, the man with black hair, is looking at his smartphone with a neutral expression. The fourth character, the man with orange hair, is holding his smartphone in one hand. None of the characters are talking or interacting with each other.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates how smartphones, designed to enhance communication and access to information, paradoxically lead to less interpersonal interaction and more isolation among people when together in social settings.
moral_mcq:
A. Smartphones streamline communication, offering ease in staying connected but often promote distractions that undermine meaningful dialogue in social settings.

B. Smartphones brighten social settings, adding excitement, yet they often divert attention from real-life interactions to screen-based ones, diminishing genuine connection.

C. Smartphones reduce face-to-face engagement and alter the dynamics of conversation among people.

D. Traditional chats are rarer and less spontaneous, with smartphones taking over, ironically turning timeless interactions into detached experiences.
title_mcq:
A. The Shift of Dialogue Dynamics
 

B. Conversations Before and After Smartphones
 

C. The Effect of Digital Devices
 

D. Engaging in the Virtual Sphere
social_info:
1. **Social Interaction Before Smartphones**: Before the widespread use of smartphones, people tended to engage more directly in face-to-face conversations, relying on each other for information and entertainment.
  
  2. **Impact of Smartphones on Social Dynamics**: Smartphones have significantly changed social interactions, often leading to individuals being more absorbed in their devices than engaging with the people physically present around them.
  
  3. **Cultural References and Knowledge Sharing**: In social settings, conversations often include sharing and discussing cultural knowledge, such as celebrities or current events, which can foster group interaction and engagement.
category: This comic depicts the shift in social interaction due to the impact of smartphones, showing how people have moved from lively discussions to isolated immersion in their digital devices.###Social media.

description:
This comic consists of two panels, each depicting a pink, fluffy, bear-like character in a living room setting over a span of three years.
  
  In the first panel, labeled "2019," the character is sitting upright on a blue couch, actively engaged with a smartphone. The room has a cheerful ambiance, highlighted by a warm yellow background and a green potted plant beside the couch. There's a festive "Happy New Year 2019" banner in the upper part of the panel, suggesting a new year's resolution or a fresh start.
  
  The second panel, labeled "2022," shows the same character three years later, lying down on the same blue couch, seemingly asleep or exhausted, with the smartphone lying beside them. The room's setup remains unchanged, indicating the passage of time without significant change in the environment. The text "2022" prominently displayed suggests another new year moment, reflecting on how the character's situation or lifestyle has barely changed over the three years, possibly hinting at procrastination or unmet goals.
  
  Overall, the comic humorously illustrates the common theme of setting ambitious new year's resolutions or goals and the often relatable outcome of not achieving them as planned, despite the passage of time.
caption:
In the first panel, a pink, rounded creature sits upright on a bright blue couch in a room with warm orange walls. A green potted plant is placed on the left side and a tall floor lamp on the right. On the wall behind the creature is a poster that reads "HAPPY NEW YEAR 2019." Above the scene, in Chinese characters, it states: “不知道3年后的现在，我会在哪里,” which in English translates to: “I don’t know where I will be three years from now.” The pink creature holds a smartphone and appears to be pondering the future.
  
  In the second panel, the same pink creature lies contentedly on the same blue couch in a room now painted yellow. A green plant still sits to the left, and the floor lamp remains on the right. On the wall behind is a poster that reads "HAPPY NEW YEAR 2022." The Chinese text reads: “3年后：很好，我还在这个房间里,” which in English translates to: “Three years later: Great, I’m still in this room.” The creature seems relaxed and at ease with the fact that not much has changed.
contradiction: The contradiction in this comic lies in the character’s initial anticipation of a different future contrasting with the comfort found in the unchanged present.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic suggests that despite new gadgets, our core habits and spaces remain unchanged, offering us comfort in the familiar instead of transformative shifts.

B. The comic implies that while technology evolves, our daily environment stays the same, reflecting satisfaction in unchanging settings rather than creating notable differences.

C. The comic illustrates that despite the passage of time and our expectations of change, we ultimately find fulfillment right where we started.

D. The comic proposes that remaining in the same environment restricts personal discovery, yet the true focus is the joy found in unchanged surroundings.
title_mcq:
A. A Decade, Same Discoveries 

B. Couch Dreams, Same Scenery 

C. Three Years, Same Couch 

D. Five Years, Same Horizons
social_info:
1. **New Year's Resolutions:** The comic plays on the common tradition of setting new goals or resolutions at the start of a new year, often with the intention of making significant life changes.
  
  2. **Procrastination and Unmet Goals:** It humorously reflects the reality that many people face‚Äîdespite good intentions, they often find themselves in the same situation years later, having not achieved their goals.
  
  3. **Passage of Time:** The unchanged environment over the years highlights how time can pass without noticeable personal progress, a relatable sentiment for many.
  
  4. **Humor and Relatability:** The comic uses humor to connect with the audience, as the scenario is a common and relatable experience.
category: The comic is a humorous critique of New Year resolutions and the reality of personal accomplishment over time.###Daily Life joke

description:
This comic illustrates the evolution of fears related to healthcare from childhood to adulthood, using two panels to depict the change in perspective.
  
  In the top panel, labeled "Childhood fear: Doctors," a young boy is shown terrified of a large syringe held by a doctor, who is partially visible. The boy, wearing a yellow shirt and blue pants, is stepping back in fear, his face expressing panic and his mouth open as if crying or shouting. The syringe, exaggerated in size to emphasize the child's fear, sparkles at the tip, indicating its sharpness and readiness for use.
  
  The bottom panel, labeled "Adult fear: Doctor's bills," shifts to the same person now grown up. The adult, wearing a similar yellow shirt, displays a subtle expression of worry and surprise as he looks at a medical bill. The bill is detailed in his hand, showing various charges like $250 for a checkup and $200 for shots, totaling $1150, highlighting the financial burdens that come with healthcare in adulthood. His expression and posture reflect concern and resignation, contrasting with the childhood fear of the actual medical procedure.
  
  Overall, the comic cleverly juxtaposes the direct fear of medical procedures in children with the adult fear of the financial implications of healthcare, using humor to reflect on how our fears evolve with our responsibilities.
caption:
The comic image is split into two panels, each depicting a different fear at different stages of life.
  
  The top panel is labeled "Childhood fear: Doctors" and shows a young boy with brown hair, wearing a yellow shirt and blue pants. He appears frightened and is backing away with his hands up, looking at a large syringe held by a doctor, who is only partially visible in the frame. The doctor's hand and the syringe are the main focus, with the needle tip sparkling.
  
  The bottom panel is labeled "Adult fear: Doctor‚Äôs bills" and features the same character, now as an adult. He has a concerned expression and is sitting, looking at a piece of paper labeled "BILL" that the doctor holds in his hands. The bill lists several charges: "CHECKUP" for $250, "SHOTS" for $200, and other unspecified items totaling $500 and $300, with an additional $150 charge. The doctor is again partially shown, this time holding the bill.
contradiction: The contradiction illustrates how the nature of our fears shifts as we age: from a childhood fear of the doctor's needle to an adult fear of the financial burden imposed by medical bills.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic humorously implies that growing older makes medical expenses seem trivial, alleviating stress from healthcare costs and making doctor's visits less intimidating over time.

B. The comic subtly hints that as we mature, the fear of healthcare providers diminishes, shifting focus to broader concerns about health and well-being.

C. The comic illustrates the evolution of fears from childhood to adulthood, from physical fears to financial worries.

D. The comic humorously indicates that with age, financial burdens feel lighter, easing anxiety about doctor visits and related healthcare expenses.
title_mcq:
A. Transforming Braces to Fears
 

B. From Needle Fear to Bill Fear
 

C. Imagination in Medical Visits
 

D. Childhood vs. Adult Projects
social_info:
1. Childhood Fear of Medical Procedures: Children often fear doctors and medical procedures like injections due to the pain or discomfort associated with them.
  
  2. Adult Financial Responsibility: Adults frequently face anxiety and stress over financial burdens, such as medical bills, due to the high cost of healthcare services.
  
  3. Evolution of Fears: As people grow, their fears shift from physical discomfort to financial and practical concerns, reflecting increased responsibilities.
  
  4. Healthcare System Costs: Understanding that healthcare can be expensive, and managing these costs is a common concern for adults, especially in countries without universal healthcare.
category: This comic belongs to the category of Health&Fitness based humor, which comically depicts the evolution of healthcare-related fears from childhood to adulthood through two panels that contrast the fear of medical procedures in children and the financial implications of healthcare in adults.###Health&Fitness

description:

caption:
