  Panel 1: (Past)
  • A student with a disappointed expression stands in front of their parents and teacher.
  • The parents are angrily questioning the child about their grade, saying “你给我解释清楚!” (“You explain this to me!”).
  • The teacher is holding a report card showing a grade of “D” or “F”.
  • The focus of blame is on the child for the bad grade.
  
  Panel 2: (Present)
  • The same situation is shown, but the dynamic has changed.
  • Now, the parents are angrily questioning the teacher, saying “你给我解释清楚!” (“You explain this to me!”).
  • The teacher looks worried while holding the same report card with a “D” or “F” grade.
  • The blame has shifted from the child to the teacher, reflecting a change in attitudes over time.

description:
First Panel:
  
  • The setting is a calm, quiet night with a crescent moon and stars twinkling in the sky, giving the impression of a peaceful neighborhood.
  • The two raccoons, anthropomorphized (walking on two legs and speaking), are standing near some bushes under the dark sky. They appear to be having a thoughtful and somewhat serious conversation.
  • The raccoon on the left, looking slightly concerned, asks:
  “我们为什么总半夜偷东西？”
  (Why do we always steal things at midnight?)
  • The raccoon on the right, standing casually with its hands in front, calmly replies:
  “坏人都是半夜行动。”
  (Bad guys always act at midnight.)
  • Their expressions are serious, as if discussing a matter of strategy, but the situation is humorous because raccoons themselves are often mischievous and stereotypically associated with sneaky nighttime behavior.
  
  Second Panel:
  
  • The scene continues in the same nighttime setting, maintaining the calm and serene mood. The crescent moon and stars are still visible in the background, highlighting the late-night atmosphere.
  • The raccoon on the left now adds another observation:
  “要是吓到别人就不好了。”
  (If we scare others, it wouldn’t be good.)
  • This suggests a strange sense of consideration from the raccoons despite their sneaky behavior.
  • The raccoon on the right responds with a simple agreement:
  “那倒是。”
  (That’s true.)
  • The raccoon appears slightly resigned but understanding.
  
  
  The humor and contradiction arise from the raccoons’ self-awareness about sneaking around at night. While they try to justify their actions by saying bad guys operate at night, they ironically express concern about scaring others—suggesting that they are trying to act “responsibly” even while doing something wrong.

description:
This comic features a humorous exchange between a human and a bear in a classroom setting, playing with the translation and meaning of a phrase.
  1. First Panel:
  • A woman (the teacher) angrily exclaims “老天不公” in Chinese, which means “God is unfair” or “The heavens are unjust.”
  • The bear, sitting at a desk like a student, listens intently, looking calm and composed.
  2. Second Panel:
  • The bear confidently translates the phrase into “God is a girl” (a humorous mistranslation of the word “不公,” which sounds phonetically like “girl” in some accents).
  • The bear looks delighted, with a smug, triumphant grin, while the teacher sits awkwardly, sweating nervously at the bear’s incorrect but confident response.
  
The contradiction lies in if the bear translates the phrase verbatim, it will lead to a complete error in translation.

  1. First Panel:
  • A character stands on a hilltop, determinedly shouting into the mountains:

  (“Starting today, I will no longer be trash!”).
  • The character looks determined, clutching its chest in a pose of resolution, as if proclaiming its desire to improve and leave behind its bad habits or negative self-view.
  2. Second Panel:
  • The scene zooms out to show the bear still standing on the hill, looking expectantly at the mountains.

description:
This two-panel comic presents a humorous take on curiosity and imagination regarding what lies beyond the visible.
  1. First Panel:
  • A raccoon sits outside on a wooden porch at night, sipping a warm drink and gazing at the moon in the sky.
  • The raccoon wonders out loud: “月亮的背面长什么样呢?” (“Hmm… What’s behind the moon?”).
  • The scene is serene and calm, with a beautiful starry night sky and a bright, smiling moon, which adds a sense of wonder to the raccoon’s innocent question.
  2. Second Panel:
  • The raccoon, still sitting and looking up, thinks aloud: “肯定也很美吧。” (“Must be beautiful.”).
  • However, the comic reveals the backside of the moon, humorously depicted with a sleeping, round moon figure holding its knees like a tired, scruffy person. The backside is far from majestic or “beautiful” as the raccoon imagines — instead, it appears mundane and relatable.
  • This unexpected visual twist contrasts the raccoon’s romanticized imagination with a comical, “down-to-earth” reality.
  
  The contradiction lies between expectation and reality. The raccoon imagines the back of the moon to be something beautiful and mysterious, but the comic humorously reveals an ordinary, tired-looking moon figure, shattering the raccoon’s romanticized vision.

description:
This two-panel comic humorously plays on a literal interpretation of a pig’s desire to look wealthy through a tattoo.
  1. First Panel: A pig lies on a table while a pig tattoo artist asks, “纹个什么?” (“What tattoo would you like?”). The lying pig confidently responds, “我想看起来很有钱” (“I want to look rich”). The scene sets up the pig’s desire to project an image of wealth through its appearance.
  2. Second Panel: The tattoo artist begins tattooing a money slot (like that of a piggy bank) onto the pig’s back. The pig looks relaxed, oblivious to the irony that it is being turned into a literal piggy bank — a humorous twist on its request to “look rich.”
  
  The contradiction lies in the pig’s intention versus the outcome. The pig wants a tattoo to make it look wealthy, but instead, the tattoo artist humorously interprets this wish by turning the pig into a literal piggy bank, a play on both its appearance and the concept of wealth.

description:
This two-panel comic humorously plays with the stereotype of sharks being drawn to the scent of blood, but subverts expectations with an unexpected twist.
  1. First Panel: A small fish warns an otter, saying:
  “你流血了，要小心哦，鲨鱼能在很远的地方闻到血腥味”
  (“You’re bleeding, be careful! Sharks can smell blood from very far away.”).
  The otter looks concerned, indicating the expected danger of a shark approaching.
  2. Second Panel: A shark appears, but instead of looking menacing, it casually holds out a band-aid and cheerfully says:
  “有人需要创可贴吗?”
  (“Does anyone need a band-aid?”).
  The shark’s friendly demeanor and helpful attitude humorously contradict its usual portrayal as a bloodthirsty predator.
  
  The contradiction lies in the expectation versus reality. Sharks are typically feared for their blood-sensing predatory instincts, but here, the shark instead arrives with a kind offer to help by providing a band-aid. This unexpected twist subverts the audience’s expectations in a lighthearted and comical way.

description:
This two-panel comic humorously plays on mistaken identity through a visual gag involving a snake and a garden hose.
  1. First Panel: A snake stands facing a coiled green garden hose. The snake says, “哇，这位漂亮姑娘，你为何如此悲伤?” (“Wow, beautiful lady, why are you so sad?”). The snake mistakes the garden hose for another snake, giving a sense of humor through its obliviousness.
  2. Second Panel: A rat appears and casually tells the snake, “亲，那是水管。” (“Buddy, that’s a water hose.”). The snake looks dejected and embarrassed, as it realizes its mistake.
  
  The contradiction lies in the snake’s assumption versus reality. The snake perceives the garden hose as a fellow snake, treating it with emotion and concern, only to have the rat bluntly reveal the truth, turning the heartfelt interaction into an awkward moment.

description:
This two-panel comic humorously captures an exaggerated emotional reaction between friends while discussing a sad scenario.
  1. First Panel: The cat and rabbit are sitting together, with the cat holding a tablet and crying. The cat says, “我刷到剧情是朋友去世的剪辑，如果是你死了我真的受不了” (“I came across a clip where a friend died in the storyline; if it were you, I really wouldn’t be able to handle it”). The rabbit, moved by the sentiment, replies, “你一哭我也想哭了” (“When you cry, it makes me want to cry too”). The emotional tone is set with a bright yellow background.
  2. Second Panel: The mood shifts to humor as the cat, still crying, says, “我明天模拟一下你死了的世界，提前习惯习惯” (“Tomorrow, I’ll simulate a world where you’re dead to get used to it in advance”). The rabbit, now looking both annoyed and unimpressed, stands silently, glaring at the cat. The background shifts to a pale purple, emphasizing the change in tone.
  
  The contradiction lies in the shift from genuine, heartfelt emotion in the first panel to absurdity in the second. While the cat initially appears deeply affected by the thought of losing the rabbit, it humorously overthinks the situation by deciding to “practice” living without the rabbit, turning the sentiment into a comedic exaggeration.

description:
This two-panel comic humorously captures a misunderstanding about sharing food.
  1. First Panel: The cat holds a partially eaten sugar-coated hawthorn skewer (“糖葫芦”) and asks the rabbit, “糖葫芦剩了一大半没吃完，你吃吗?” (“The sugar-coated hawthorn is more than half uneaten. Do you want it?”). The rabbit, excited, responds enthusiastically, “我要吃!” (“I want it!”).
  2. Second Panel: The cat casually explains, “我只把外面那层糖吃了” (“I only ate the outer layer of sugar”), holding the skewer of plain hawthorn berries. The rabbit, realizing the cat left behind only the sour, unsweetened part, looks angry and frustrated, exclaiming, “那就不是糖葫芦了，只是一串山楂啊!” (“That’s not sugar-coated hawthorn anymore, it’s just a skewer of hawthorn!”).
  
  
  The contradiction lies in the expectation versus reality of the shared food. The rabbit eagerly agrees to eat the “sugar-coated hawthorn,” expecting a sweet treat, but is disappointed to find that the cat has eaten all the sugar, leaving only the plain hawthorn berries. This humorous mismatch highlights the gap between what was offered and what was actually shared.

description:
This comic strip tells a whimsical and imaginative story involving two cat characters. Here's a detailed breakdown of the narrative:
  
  1. **First Panel**: The scene opens in a dark, cave-like setting where a majestic cat adorned with a crown and royal attire sits on a throne made of stone, looking quite displeased and regal. Water drips around it, adding to the somber ambiance. A simpler, smaller gray cat looks on, seemingly in awe or curiosity of the royal cat's demeanor and setting.
  
  2. **Second Panel**: The focus shifts to the gray cat, who now wields a large, glowing blue sword. This sword seems to have magical properties, as it emits light and energy. The royal cat watches from the throne, its expression now showing a mix of surprise and interest.
  
  3. **Third Panel**: The narrative takes an unexpected turn as the scene changes to a cozy domestic setting. The gray cat, still equipped with the magical sword, is now using it in a mundane, everyday situation: cooking. The cat is slicing what appears to be fish with the sword, while other typical kitchen items like a pot of soup and condiments are laid out on the table.
  
  This comic cleverly juxtaposes the fantastical elements of a magical sword and a royal cat with the ordinary task of cooking dinner. The humor lies in the absurdity and unexpectedness of using a powerful artifact for such a simple, everyday activity, highlighting a playful blend of epic and mundane themes.

This two-panel comic humorously depicts the escalating burden of responsibility.
  1. First Panel: Titled “责任越大” (“The bigger the responsibility”), a rabbit is seen handing a task (clipboard) to a carrot character. The carrot reluctantly says, “交给我吧” (“Give it to me”), while the rabbit eagerly says, “交给你咯” (“Leaving it to you”). The lighthearted tone suggests the carrot is taking on a manageable responsibility.
  2. Second Panel: Titled “责任就会越来越大” (“Responsibilities will keep growing bigger”), the carrot is now visibly overwhelmed and stressed. More characters—a goose, a dog, and a cat—each hand additional tasks (documents) to the carrot, with the cat saying, “这些你也做了吧” (“You can do these as well”). A pile of papers grows beside the carrot, emphasizing the crushing weight of increasing responsibilities.
  
  The contradiction lies in the carrot’s willingness to take on a small task in the first panel versus its overwhelmed state in the second panel. While the carrot starts by accepting responsibility, the growing demands humorously illustrate how small responsibilities can snowball into unmanageable burdens.

  The contradiction lies in the cat’s serious call to “seize opportunities” in the first panel versus its trivial, self-serving application of this principle to indulging in food in the second panel, humorously exposing the gap between ideals and actions.

  The contradiction lies in the cat’s ridiculous and illogical excuse. The task of pushing a shopping cart on solid ground has nothing to do with motion sickness, making its response both absurd and comically lazy. This highlights the cat’s unwillingness to share the workload, despite the rabbit’s clear exhaustion, and exaggerates the lengths to which someone might go to avoid responsibility.

description:
This two-panel comic humorously depicts a dog attempting to exercise for health benefits, but with minimal effort and exaggerated expectations.
  1. First Panel: The dog is lying on a yoga mat, casually holding a pair of tiny dumbbells and lifting them lazily. It says enthusiastically, “运动健身延年益寿!” (“Exercise prolongs life and brings health benefits!”). In the background, there is a carrot-shaped jump rope and another dog struggling to perform a push-up, comically exaggerating the struggle of fitness.
  2. Second Panel: The background changes to a gym-like setting with a purple tone. A cheerful rabbit is holding dumbbells and says to the dog, “你只举了一下耶” (“You only lifted once”). The dog smugly responds, “应该能多活一分钟吧!” (“That should help me live one more minute, right?”), implying that the minimal effort was enough to achieve major health benefits. Meanwhile, a cat is hanging from a punching bag in the background, struggling to stay up.
  
  The contradiction lies in the disparity between the effort put into exercising and the expected outcome. The dog’s minimal and lazy attempt at lifting weights contrasts humorously with its grand expectation of significantly improving its health and longevity. This exaggeration highlights a comedic take on people who expect big results from very little effort.

description:
This comic is a humorous two-panel depiction of eating habits before and after attempting weight loss.
  1. First Panel: Titled “减肥前的食量” (“Food intake before weight loss”), it shows a chubby character sitting at a desk with a modest meal consisting of a hamburger, fries, and a drink. The character looks calm and content while eating.
  2. Second Panel: Titled “减肥后的食量” (“Food intake after weight loss”), it humorously exaggerates the aftermath of dieting. The same character is now frantically eating a massive assortment of food, including noodles, fried chicken, cupcakes, snacks, multiple bowls, and drinks, completely covering the desk. The character appears sweaty, overwhelmed, and ravenously devouring everything in sight.
  
  Contradiction:
  
  The contradiction lies in the expectation versus reality of dieting. While dieting is often associated with reducing food intake, the comic humorously suggests that the effort to restrict eating (“减肥”) can lead to a rebound effect, where the person ends up consuming far more food than before. This exaggeration highlights the difficulty of maintaining self-control and the common struggle of overcompensating after a period of restriction.

description:
This comic is a two-panel cartoon featuring a dog and a cat interacting humorously.
  1. First Panel: The cat is depicted as cute and cheerful, with a smiling face and a pink background adorned with small heart icons. The dog, who looks skeptical and serious, uses one paw to touch the cat’s face and says, “让我看看你的真面目” (“Let me see your true face”). The cat maintains its happy and innocent demeanor.
  2. Second Panel: The background changes to a darker purple tone, indicating a shift in mood. The dog is now holding what appears to be a removable mask that looks like the cat’s cheerful face, revealing a mischievous and sly version of the cat underneath. The cat, with its real face now exposed, says, “今天犯点什么剑呢” (“What kind of mischief should I cause today?”), while the dog responds, “我就知道” (“I knew it”).
  
  The contradiction lies in the contrast between appearances and reality. In the first panel, the cat presents an innocent and lovable front, symbolized by its cheerful expression and the lighthearted background. However, in the second panel, the cat’s true nature is revealed to be mischievous and devious, as indicated by its sly expression and the darker tone. This humorous contradiction highlights the theme of deceptive appearances and the idea that things may not be as they initially seem.

  In the first panel, the cat energetically exclaims, “是时候规划我的未来了！” (“It’s time to plan my future!”) while holding a red pen in the air. The background is bright yellow with rays radiating outward, symbolizing enthusiasm and determination.
  
  In the second panel, the cat is shown lying on the ground with a big smile, still holding the red pen, as it writes something on a piece of paper, and it declares, “等我死了要用粉色的骨灰盒装我，坟头草就种西兰花吧。理由：可爱” (“When I die, I want to be buried in a pink urn, and I want broccoli to be planted on my grave. Reason: Cute”).
  The green background and the cat’s relaxed posture create a humorous contrast to the “serious” topic it is planning.
  
  The contradiction lies in the disparity between the cat’s initial enthusiastic declaration to “plan its future” and the unexpectedly whimsical and lighthearted nature of its plan, which focuses entirely on its burial rather than practical life goals. 
  
  This twist humorously highlights the cat’s quirky logic and playful attitude, subverting the reader’s expectations of what “future planning” typically entails.

description:
This comic illustrates the evolution of comfort and intimacy in a relationship over time, depicted through two contrasting panels labeled "The First Month" and "After 1 Year."
  
  In the first panel, titled "The First Month," a woman in a red bikini is sitting on a couch, covering herself with her arms and asking a man standing nearby to "Turn around, I'm shy!" The man, dressed in a grey sweater and black pants, looks surprised but respectful of her request. This scene captures the initial stages of a relationship where there is still a significant level of shyness and reserve.
  
  In the second panel, titled “After 1 Year,” the scene shifts to a more casual and humorous setting. The woman, dressed in a casual white top with flour smeared on her belly, is sitting at a table with a bag of flour. She cheerfully says, “Look what I can do!” as she playfully tosses flour from her hand, creating a puff of white dust. The man, standing nearby and dressed similarly to the first panel, watches with a slightly confused and bemused expression. This panel highlights the comfort and playfulness that develop in relationships over time, showing how partners become more uninhibited and relaxed with each other.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the dramatic shift in the girl’s attitude toward the same type of situation as the relationship progresses, changing from trustful curiosity to suspicious jealousy.

description:
The comic consists of two panels showing how a couple’s sleeping habits evolve over time.
  
  In the first panel, titled “THE FIRST MONTH,” the couple is shown sleeping very carefully together. The man and woman are both visibly uncomfortable, sweating nervously, and lying stiffly next to each other in an awkward spooning position. The man’s arm is placed gently around the woman, but both seem overly tense and wide-eyed, unsure of how to position themselves comfortably.
  
  In the second panel, titled “AFTER 1 YEAR,” the situation changes drastically. The woman is sleeping soundly and sprawled across the bed in a starfish position, using the man as a pillow. Her arms and legs drape over him, while the man lies flat on his back, clearly squished but sleeping peacefully. Small heart symbols float above them, indicating comfort and affection despite the chaotic arrangement.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in how the couple’s sleeping dynamic shifts from overly cautious and reserved to completely unrestrained and relaxed over time.

description:
This comic humorously highlights how a girl’s behavior changes between the beginning of a relationship and after a long time together:
  
  In the first panel, titled “THE FIRST MONTH,” the girl appears delicate and helpless, handing a jar to the boy with an innocent expression. She says, “It’s so tough I can’t open it.” The boy, with a confident smile, steps in to help, feeling strong and protective. This reflects how, in the early days of a relationship, the girl pretends to be weak and dependent.
  
  In the second panel, titled “AFTER 1 YEAR,” the situation is completely different. The girl is effortlessly lifting one side of a heavy couch with one hand while vacuuming with the other. The boy, sitting on the couch, looks shocked and bewildered as he realizes the girl’s true strength. By this point in the relationship, the girl no longer hides her abilities or strength.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in how the girl initially pretends to be weak but eventually reveals her true strength once the relationship matures.

description:
In the first panel, a red balloon is stuck in a tree, causing distress to a fluffy white character, who cries dramatically. A gray character looks on indifferently, while a beaver stands nearby with a calm, knowing expression.
  
  In the second panel, the beaver springs into action, gnawing through the tree trunk with incredible speed and force. The fluffy white character now appears excited and in awe, while the gray character continues to watch with an unbothered demeanor.
  
  In the third panel, the tree has been completely severed and lies on the ground, but the red balloon has floated even higher out of reach. The fluffy white character now looks dejected, while the beaver scratches its head in confusion. Meanwhile, a blue balloon floats nearby, unnoticed by everyone.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the effort and destruction caused by the beaver's solution, which ultimately fails to solve the problem, leaving the balloon even more inaccessible.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the shift from the girl’s initial efforts to appear reserved and healthy to her unabashed enjoyment of food as the relationship progresses.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the difference between someone’s outward physical state, which appears normal, and their emotional state, which is frozen or numb.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the disparity between ambitious plans (exercising together) and the often lazy or unmotivated reality (sleeping instead).

  In the second panel, the comic takes the term “buss” literally. Dishes, food, and other workers are flying in all directions as they panic, creating a comically exaggerated and chaotic scene.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the employee's misinterpretation of "buss," leading to an absurd and literal outcome instead of the expected task of clearing tables.

description:
This comic humorously illustrates the paradoxical behavior of pets and their relationship with their owners.
  
  In the first panel, titled "EVERY TIME I CALL THEM," the woman is shown happily trying to get her pet ferret’s attention by playing with a ball and toys. However, the ferret ignores her and rolls on its back lazily, uninterested and oblivious to her efforts. This highlights how pets often ignore calls for attention when it suits them.
  
  In the second panel, titled "WHEN I NEED A MINUTE TO MYSELF," the woman is sitting on the toilet, clearly hoping for some privacy. However, the ferret is now desperately scratching at the bathroom door, indicated by repeated SCRATCH SCRATCH SCRATCH sound effects. The woman looks annoyed and resigned, showing how pets suddenly demand attention when they’re not wanted.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the pet’s selective attention—ignoring calls for play but becoming clingy when the owner needs time alone.

  In the first panel, titled “Beginning of dating”, the couple is shown eating together with a sweet, romantic tone. The woman smiles lovingly while holding a fork and says, “Say ahhh!” The man, looking cheerful and delighted, opens his mouth eagerly and says, “AHHH~” The scene exudes affection, care, and mutual admiration as they share food politely.
  
  In the second panel, titled “After a few years”, the same couple is shown in a dramatically different and chaotic scenario. The woman is sprawled across the couch with a bag of snacks, greedily shoving food into her mouth, crumbs flying everywhere. Meanwhile, the man desperately reaches for the snacks, yelling “GIMME SOME!!!” The woman pushes his face away with her hand, showing how the dynamic has shifted from loving gestures to playful, messy food fights over time.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the shift from polite, romantic gestures early in a relationship to unfiltered, competitive behavior once the couple becomes more comfortable with each other.

This comic humorously depicts an unexpected turn of events where survival turns into a playful ride:
  
  In the first panel, two cats cling to a floating log in a rushing river, their faces filled with panic and fear. A cheerful beaver stands on the riverbank watching the scene, clearly amused but seemingly thoughtful.
  
  In the second panel, the beaver has climbed onto the log with the terrified cats. Instead of panicking, the beaver enthusiastically chews away at the log, creating seats as if designing a ride. The cats remain tense and wide-eyed, unable to process the chaos, while the beaver looks excited and satisfied with its “improvement.”
  
  In the third panel, the log now resembles a playful ride, like one from an amusement park water attraction. The beaver throws its arms up joyfully as they plunge down a massive waterfall. The cats, having accepted their fate, no longer look terrified but instead share the beaver's excitement, treating the situation as a thrilling adventure.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in how a seemingly dangerous and life-threatening situation transforms into a fun and playful ride, thanks to the beaver's creativity and excitement.

  In the first panel, a blind man wearing sunglasses is on the phone, clearly frustrated. He says, “YOU SENT ME THE WRONG GUIDE DOG.” The situation suggests that the man has received an incorrect or dysfunctional guide dog.
  
  In the second panel, the humorous twist is revealed. The man is standing next to a talking guide dog who says, “THIS IS A MAGRITTE. PAINTED IN 1964.” The dog refers to the famous painting “The Son of Man” by René Magritte, which is visible on the wall. The painting is iconic for featuring a man in a suit with an apple obscuring his face—implying the “guide” (apple) is also obstructing the man’s vision. The joke is that instead of helping, the “guide” dog gives irrelevant art commentary.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the expectation of a helpful guide dog versus the absurd reality of a dog providing art facts instead.

description:
This comic delivers a humorous and creative twist on the concept of ostriches burying their heads in the sand:
  
  In the first panel, two ostriches are doing what ostriches are famously (and incorrectly) known for: burying their heads in the ground. Their large, fluffy bodies and legs are visible above the surface, giving the impression that their heads are deep underground.
  
  In the second panel, the twist is revealed. Instead of simply “hiding,” the ostriches’ heads have actually extended underground into a hidden bar. Their heads are poking through the ceiling, and they are sipping drinks (a martini and a mojito) through straws while relaxing at a table. The underground bar has a neon “BAR” sign, brick walls, and a third character—a mole—holding a ladder and looking surprised at the scene.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the humorous reinterpretation of ostriches “burying their heads” as secretly enjoying drinks at a hidden underground bar.

description:
This comic humorously highlights the timeless experience of spending "just a few minutes" online, which inevitably turns into an extended period of time:
  
  In the first panel, a young child sits excitedly at a desk with a computer. The child asks their mom, “Mom, can I go online?” The mom replies from off-panel, “OK, but just for a few minutes.” The scene suggests an innocent start, where the child has been granted limited screen time.
  
  In the second panel, time has clearly passed—a lot of time. The child is now an older adult with thinning hair, glasses, and a rounded figure, but they are still sitting at the same desk, using the same computer. The adult, now aged and visibly unchanged in behavior, simply says, “OK.” The comic implies they never stopped being online, comically exaggerating how quickly time can slip away while using the internet.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the idea of going online “for a few minutes” versus the reality that hours—or even decades—can pass unnoticed.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the character's initial claim to distrust men versus their sudden and complete dependence on one moments later.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the stark difference in the bear’s mood when starting the workday calmly versus the thrill of barely avoiding lateness.

  In the first panel, four candles are anthropomorphized with human-like faces and bodies. Their flames serve as heads, and they are all holding their noses, looking disgusted and uncomfortable. The exaggerated expressions suggest they are reacting to a terrible smell.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the candles being personified and reacting like humans to something they normally "experience"—being blown out—leading to an unexpected and comical twist.

description:
This comic consists of two panels that address the concept of media influence and individual perception:
  
  In the first panel: A speaker at a podium asks the audience, "Who thinks the media controls people’s thoughts?" (translated from Chinese). In response, everyone in the audience eagerly raises their hands, appearing confident and unanimous in their belief that the media exerts control over society.
  
  In the second panel: The speaker follows up with a second question: "Who thinks they themselves are being controlled?" This time, no one raises their hand, and the audience members look down, silent, and unsure. The contradiction highlights their unwillingness to admit that they might be personally influenced.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in people recognizing that others are influenced by external forces, like the media, but refusing to acknowledge that they themselves may also be controlled.

  The contradiction in this comic lies in the initial perception of triumph versus the unexpected failure caused by a hidden, larger consequence.

description:
This comic strip comprises two panels that depict a humorous and relatable family scenario.
  
  In the left panel, we see a cozy and peaceful scene inside a home. A woman with brown hair, wearing an orange sweater and glasses, is comfortably seated on a cushion by a large window, sipping from a mug. Beside her, a small child with black hair tied up in a ponytail, dressed in a red jumper, stands by the window, looking out. The atmosphere suggests a quiet, content moment between the two, possibly during a morning or afternoon.
  
  The right panel reveals a comedic twist to the scene. From the perspective of someone outside looking in, we see that the child is actually making faces at the window. The child's face is humorously distorted against the glass, tongue out, eyes crossed, creating a stark contrast to the serene scene depicted in the first panel. The kid's tongue is sticked on the window due to cold weather. Additionally, a small bird with big eyes is perched outside, looking up at the child, adding to the whimsical and light-hearted nature of the moment.
  
  The comic effectively uses the window as a literal and metaphorical lens, showing how one peaceful scene inside can appear hilariously different from another perspective outside.

The child appears to be pressing their hand against the glass.

description:
This comic features a humorous interaction between two sea creatures, a small fish and a large shark, spread across two panels.
  
  In the left panel, the scene is set in a calm blue ocean. The small fish introduces the shark, saying, "My name's Kevin." The shark, significantly larger and depicted with a slight smile, faces the small fish. The simplicity of the background focuses attention on the dialogue and characters.
  
  In the right panel, the perspective shifts to a closer view of the shark, who continues the introduction from the first panel with, "but most people just call me..." However, instead of completing the sentence in a conventional way, the panel is filled with the repeated screams of "AAAAAAHHHHH" in large, bold letters. This humorous twist plays on the typical fear response that people might have upon seeing a shark, contrasting with the casual and friendly introduction that began with "My name's Kevin."
  
  The comic uses visual storytelling and text to create a punchline, emphasizing the juxtaposition between the shark's intended friendly introduction and the typical human reaction to a shark. The artist's use of simple drawings and clear text enhances the humor and accessibility of the joke.
caption:

  In the left panel, there are two fish depicted. On the left is a smaller fish with a simple design, featuring stripes and a basic facial expression. On the right is a much larger shark, drawn with more detail including gills, a fin, and a slightly open mouth showing teeth. Above the shark, there is a speech bubble that reads, "my name's kevin."
  
  The right panel shows the same shark, now occupying most of the panel with its mouth wide open, displaying a full set of sharp teeth and a more aggressive expression. A speech bubble in front of the shark contains the text "but most people just call me" followed by multiple lines of the text "AAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHHHHH" in a larger, bold font, indicating screaming.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the juxtaposition between the shark's calm introduction of himself as "Kevin" and the terrified reaction typically associated with sharks, represented by the screaming "AAAAAAHHHH" in the second panel. While Kevin attempts to present himself in a friendly, personable manner, the typical fear sharks inspire in others leads to a humorous and contradictory interpretation of his identity.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic humorously suggests a friendly name can't change perceptions, as core traits remain unchanged, revealing the unpredictable nature of stereotypes versus reality.

B. The comic humorously shows that understanding predators like sharks doesn't eliminate fear, illustrating how primal reactions persist regardless of intentions or appearances.

C. The comic illustrates the importance of not judging others based solely on their appearance or reputation.

D. The comic highlights humor's role in engaging with dangerous animals, implying that playfulness can reveal their essence, while pointing out inherent conflicts in perceptions.

description:
This comic image humorously contrasts the "Expectation" versus "Reality" of wearing a belt buckle styled after the Batman logo.
  
  On the left, labeled "Expectation," the panel shows a person wearing the Batman belt buckle. This side of the comic depicts an idealized version where the belt fits perfectly on a trim waist, accentuating a flat stomach. The buckle itself is prominent and stylish, suggesting a cool and heroic association with the Batman character.
  
  On the right, labeled "Reality," the comic presents a starkly different scenario. Here, the person wearing the same Batman belt buckle appears to have a fuller figure. The belt buckle digs uncomfortably into the stomach, causing the skin to bulge over and around it. This creates an image where the Batman logo looks like it's grimacing or being distorted by the pressure, which adds a humorous and slightly exaggerated touch to the reality of wearing such a themed accessory on a less than ideal body type.
  
  Overall, the comic uses exaggerated visual elements to playfully critique how certain fashion items, like themed belt buckles, might not always meet the expectations set by popular culture and media.

description:
The comic humorously reflects a bear's internal monologue about rest.
  
  In the first panel, the bear lies in bed wide-eyed, staring at the ceiling. The text above reads: “难道我要眼睁睁地浪费掉光阴吗” ("Am I just going to waste time lying here with my eyes wide open?"). The bear’s face is filled with worry and existential frustration.
  
  In the second panel, the bear closes its eyes peacefully with a smile, tucked comfortably under the blanket. The large text says: “不” ("No"), and the smaller text adds: “我会闭上眼” ("I’ll close my eyes"). The bear appears satisfied with its decision to rest.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the bear's dramatic inner struggle about wasting time, humorously resolved by simply going to sleep.

description:
This comic features a humorous misunderstanding between two characters, likely a couple, communicated through text messages and their subsequent weekend activity. 
  
  In the first panel, the female character, holding her smartphone, texts the male character, "Hey dear," to which he replies, "Heyy." She then asks, "What are we doing this weekend?" In the next panel, the male character, excitedly holding his phone, responds, "I bought the new BMW, let's try it together." The female character, misunderstanding "BMW" to refer to a car, exclaims in surprise and delight, "BMW???" to which he confirms, "Yeah!"
  
  The punchline of the comic is revealed in the large panel labeled "THAT WEEKEND:" where the misunderstanding is clarified. Instead of a new car, "BMW" refers to a video game titled "Black Myth: Wukong," as indicated by the game's logo and artwork displayed on the television screen. The male character is shown enthusiastically playing the game with a gaming controller and headphones, while the female character sits beside him on the couch, looking disappointed and cross-armed, clearly not what she had expected for their weekend.
caption:

  1. The first panel shows two frames. In the left frame, a woman with short brown hair, wearing a blue tank top, is holding a smartphone and texting. The text bubble says, "Hey dear" followed by a response "Heyy". In the right frame, she asks, "What are we doing this weekend?" The response from the other person is, "I bought the new BMW, let‚Äôs try it together." She replies with surprise, "BMW???" and the other person confirms, "Yeah!"
  
  2. The second panel is labeled "THAT WEEKEND:" and depicts the woman and a man sitting in a living room. The woman, looking displeased with her arms crossed, is sitting on a green sofa. The man, wearing a red sleeveless shirt and white headphones, is enthusiastically playing a video game holding a controller. The background shows a dark room illuminated by the light from a TV screen.
  
  3. The third panel features the text "BLACK MYTH WUKONG" prominently at the top, suggesting the name of the video game being played. The artwork within this panel shows a character resembling a warrior in traditional armor, wielding a staff, which corresponds to the theme of the game mentioned.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the difference between expectations and reality in communication. The woman expects that they will be going out to test drive a new BMW car over the weekend, but the reality is that they end up playing the "Black Myth: Wukong" video game,
moral_mcq:
A. The comic humorously shows that weekends in video games can unlock unexpected creativity, promising intellectual growth, skill enhancement, and profound perspectives, despite reality sometimes not aligning with such narratives.

B. The comic illustrates the importance of clear communication and managing expectations in relationships.

C. The comic suggests that purchasing BMWs as a shared activity will undoubtedly lead to stronger connections, enriching relationships, and fostering unity despite having different interests.

D. The comic portrays that gaming with partners invariably leads to excitement and memorable experiences, ensuring relationships stay dynamic and stimulating, no matter the differing expectations.
title_mcq:
A. Unexpected Adventure Retreat 

B. Weekend Plans Gone Gaming 

C. Anticipated Drive Thrill 

D. Calm Indoor Expectations
social_info:
1. **Acronym Ambiguity**: The acronym "BMW" is commonly known as a luxury car brand, but it can also stand for different things, leading to misunderstandings.
  
  2. **Expectations in Relationships**: Couples often have different expectations for shared activities, and communication is key to avoid disappointments.

description:
In the first panel, a cheerful bear looks at a pregnant woman and says, “真羡慕你啊” ("I really envy you"). The woman smiles and asks, “你也想要宝宝吗” ("Do you also want a baby?").
  
  In the second panel, the bear, with a playful and slightly wistful expression, touches the woman’s belly and says, “我想当宝宝” ("I want to be the baby"). The bear is expressing a longing to return to the state of being a cared-for, innocent little baby, rather than any desire to have or take care of a child.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the woman assuming the bear wants to have a child, while the bear instead wishes to return to being a baby itself.

description:
This comic strip features two panels, each depicting a humorous interaction between a human and a chubby, anthropomorphic bear-like creature wearing a small hat.
  
  In the left panel, (labeled 「拜托别人七点叫醒我」 which means “I asked someone to wake me up at 7 o’clock”): A plump, bear-like hamster wearing a small hat politely pleads with another person. The hamster’s posture is relaxed yet hopeful, clearly expecting help in waking up on time.
  
  In the right panel, (labeled 「别人七点叫醒我」 meaning “Someone woke me up at 7 o’clock”): The hamster now looks grumpy and annoyed, even though the other person did exactly as requested. Tiny white text near the hamster reads 「谢谢 真准时」, translating to “Thank you, very punctual,” dripping with sarcasm.
  
  The comic illustrates that even when we get precisely what we ask for, we may not be prepared for the reality of it.

description:
This comic image captures a humorous and relatable moment in family life, contrasting the polished image often presented on social media with the chaotic reality of parenting.
  
  On the left side of the image, we see a smartphone screen displaying a photo that a woman has presumably posted online. In this photo, she is smiling broadly, looking polished and happy, standing in a tidy room. She holds a small child in her arms who is also smiling and appears well-behaved. The scene is picture-perfect, akin to many social media posts where people share idealized snapshots of their life.
  
  On the right side of the image, we see the reality behind the camera. The same woman, now looking exhausted and frazzled, is sprawled on the floor in a messy room. Another child, who is not in the social media photo, is playfully causing chaos around her. This child wears a pot as a hat, splashes paint everywhere, and seems to be thoroughly enjoying the mess. Toys and household items are scattered all over the floor, depicting a scene of disarray and the everyday challenges of parenting.
  
  This comic cleverly juxtaposes the curated, flawless images people often choose to share online with the less polished, more authentic experiences of daily life. It highlights the often humorous disparity between perception and reality in the age of social media.
caption:
The image is a split comic illustration that depicts two contrasting scenes related to parenting. On the left side, the scene is shown within the frame of a smartphone screen, suggesting it is a photo being taken. It features a woman and a young boy smiling at the camera. The woman has long, dark hair and is wearing a red top. The boy, who appears happy, is wearing a green shirt and jeans. Below them, on the smartphone screen, are icons typically associated with a social media app, including a heart and a comment icon.
  
  On the right side of the comic, outside the smartphone frame, the scene is chaotic and messy. Another child, wearing a bucket on his head as a hat, decorated with a flower sticker, is joyfully splashing paint everywhere with a paintbrush. The child is wearing a paint-splattered shirt and pants. The background is filled with various objects in disarray, including a spilled paint bucket, a cat being splashed with paint, toys, and dirty dishes scattered around. The woman from the left side is also depicted here, looking exhausted and overwhelmed, with her hair up in a messy bun and her hand on her forehead.
  
  This comic visually contrasts the polished, idealized image shown on social media with the more chaotic, real-life experience of parenting.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the disparity between the curated perfection shown in social media posts and the often chaotic reality of everyday life. While the image on the phone displays a mother and child smiling as if everything is under control, the actual scene is chaotic with the child making a mess in the room, highlighting the selective sharing on social media platforms.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic portrays an illusion where children always seem joyful, crafting scenes of endless familial happiness and ideal moments, ignoring everyday chaos and real emotions.

B. The comic suggests social media accurately depicts daily life, showing true family dynamics without distortion, capturing both harmony and disorder as they naturally occur.

C. The comic illustrates the contrast between reality and the idealized versions of life often depicted on social media.

D. The comic implies that a spotless environment equates to a peaceful family life, emphasizing cleanliness as vital for maintaining a balanced existence.
title_mcq:
A. Calm Indoor Chaos 

B. Picture Perfect Chaos 

C. Tranquil Home Turmoil 

D. Silent Park Pandemonium
social_info:
1. **Social Media Curation**: Understanding that people often post idealized versions of their lives on social media, which may not reflect reality.
  
  2. **Parenting Challenges**: Recognizing the everyday chaos and challenges that come with parenting, which are often not shown in curated social media posts.
  
  3. **Perception vs. Reality**: The concept that what is shown online can be very different from real life, highlighting the disparity between appearance and reality.
category: This comic vividly illustrates the misrepresentation of parenity on social media, comically showcasing the disparity between polished online posts and the messier realities of parenting.###Social media

description:
The comic strip portrays a humorous and absurd situation involving three characters. In the upper panel, one character is holding another who appears to be injured, with a visible blood stain on his shirt. A third character runs towards them, proclaiming, "I can help!"
  
  In the lower panel, the person assisting the injured man asks the newcomer if he is a doctor, to which the latter cheerfully replies, "I'm an artist."
  
  The final panel reveals the artist's method of 'helping'‚ he uses a red marker to draw a smiley face over the injured man's blood stain, implying a comedic yet ineffective solution to the situation. The expressions and body language of the characters add to the absurdity and humor of the scene, showcasing the artist's misplaced enthusiasm in a critical moment.
caption:
The comic consists of three panels set against a light blue background. Each panel includes speech bubbles.
  
  1. The first panel shows three characters. On the left, a man with a beard and a worried expression is kneeling and supporting another man who is lying on the ground, appearing unconscious with a small red blood stain on his shirt. A third man, wearing glasses and appearing enthusiastic, is running towards them saying, "I can help!"
  
  2. The second panel focuses on the kneeling man looking up at the man with glasses, who has now approached them. The kneeling man asks, "Are you a doctor?" The man with glasses responds, "I'm an artist."
  
  3. The third panel shows the artist holding a red marker, having drawn two red circles on the eyes of the unconscious man, making him look like a cartoon character. The kneeling man looks on, puzzled and concerned.
contradiction: The contradiction illustrates the disparity between the urgent medical help needed and the type of assistance offered. While one character urgently declares that a man is bleeding to death, another character offers help but reveals he is an artist, not a medically trained professional, thus humorously highlighting his inability to provide the necessary medical intervention.
moral_mcq:
A. Artistic ideas can provide fresh perspectives to urgent situations. However, imagination can't replace necessary skills when urgent expertise is needed for life-threatening problems.

B. The comic illustrates the importance of having the right skills for specific situations.

C. Anyone can creatively approach complex scenarios, seeking innovation in adversity. Yet subjective genius isn’t a substitute for immediate skills in urgent, life-threatening cases.

D. Creative expression through unexpected means offers new solutions. Yet such methods fail to meet urgent needs when specific, life-saving expertise is crucial.
title_mcq:
A. Brushes’ Scrubs 

B. Vibrant Aid 

C. Artistic First Aid 

D. Palette Helper
social_info:
1. **Emergency Situations**: In critical situations, such as someone bleeding, professional medical help is needed. People often expect someone offering help to have relevant expertise, like being a doctor.
  
  2. **Role of Professionals**: Different professions have specific skills. A doctor is trained to handle medical emergencies, while an artist is not, highlighting the humor in the artist's misplaced confidence.
category: This comic strip belongs to the category of situational humor, presenting an absurd scenario in a critical situation where an artist tries to 'help' an injured man in a very unconventional and humorous way.###Situational Humor

  In the second panel, titled “我的脑子” ("My Brain"), the scene shifts to show the bear’s brain tucked cozily in bed, snoozing peacefully under a blanket, ignoring the bear's enthusiasm. Outside the window, the bear is still yelling, “干翻世界!” ("Conquer the world!"), but its brain remains unbothered and asleep.
  
  The contradiction in this comic lies in the disconnect between the bear’s motivated intentions and its brain’s refusal to cooperate by staying asleep.

description:
The comic image features a humorous sequence involving two cats and their interaction with a chessboard. The narrative unfolds in three panels:
  
  In the left panel, Two cats are shown, each eating from separate bowls placed on the floor. This panel sets up a peaceful, everyday scene where the cats are engaged in a typical activity. This panel introduces an element of play and interaction between the two cats, using the chessboard as a medium.
  
  In the right panel, The chessboard is now fully revealed with numerous chess pieces knocked over, indicating a playful or chaotic interaction rather than an actual game of chess. One cat is actively pushing a paw through the board while the other watches. This panel highlights the cats' playful nature and their indifference to the conventional use of the chessboard, turning it into a toy rather than a game platform.
  
  Overall, the comic portrays a light-hearted and amusing interpretation of how pets can transform ordinary objects into sources of entertainment and interaction, reflecting their curious and playful characteristics.
caption:

  1. In the top panel, two cats are shown from the side, each eating from separate bowls placed in front of them on the ground.
  
  2. The middle panel depicts the same two cats, now facing each other. One cat is stretching its paw through a grid drawn on the floor between them, touching the other cat's paw that is also stretched out.
  
  3. In the bottom panel, the two cats are sitting opposite each other at a table that has a chessboard on it. One cat appears to be moving a chess piece on the board, while the other watches. Each cat has a bowl of food beside them on the floor.
  
  The artist's signature, "TANGO 2010", is visible at the bottom right corner of the image.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the unexpected transformation of a mundane activity into a strategic game. Initially, the cats are simply eating from their bowls, but the scene humorously escalates as they use their food to play a game of checkers, blending the ordinary act of feeding with the intellectual challenge of a board game.

description:
The comic image consists of two panels, each depicting a humorous scenario involving a cute, anthropomorphic bear character in a role-playing game setting.
  
  In the left panel, the bear appears delighted and ready for battle, equipped with a small shield and a club. The bear is facing a very small, harmless-looking green slime creature, which is a common low-level enemy in many role-playing games. The text above them reads "The diffuclt level of my work" ("工作的难度") and a small health bar above the slime shows it is at level 1. The bear confidently says, "That's it?" (”就这？“) indicating its readiness to fight what it perceives as an easy opponent.
  
  In the right panel, the scene dramatically shifts to show the bear now facing a much larger and menacing monster, which resembles a giant, angry hippopotamus with sharp teeth and a small creature on its back. The bear, maintaining its battle stance, throws the club towards the fearsome opponent in a comedic underestimation of the threat. The text changes to "The diffcult level of getting ready to work," ("收拾心情去工作的难度") humorously juxtaposing the bear's initial overconfidence with the daunting reality of a much tougher challenge. The bear's expression and action comically underscore its unpreparedness for the escalated difficulty level.

description:
This four-panel comic depicts a humorous and slightly surreal situation involving a person and their nighttime experiences.
  
  In the left panel, we see a person sleeping peacefully in their bed, covered with a blue blanket. Their expression is calm, indicating a deep sleep. Then a creepy, humanoid creature with a featureless, brown appearance is hiding under the bed. This creature is reaching out towards the sleeping person, adding a sense of impending disturbance.
  
  In the right panel, Instead of harming the sleeper, the creature gently lifts the blanket and tucks the person in more snugly. The sleeper, still oblivious and undisturbed, now has their arms above the blanket, maintaining a peaceful expression. He opens his blanket and invite the creature to sleep with him. The creature, having tucked the person in, now lies beside them, mimicking a cuddling position. The person, still asleep, has a content smile, and a heart symbol appears above them, suggesting they are feeling loved and secure, even in the presence of what initially seemed like a menacing figure.

description:
This comic strip unfolds in four panels, each depicting a humorous and slightly surreal scenario involving a man and a large block of ice.
  
  In the left panel, we see a man standing next to a massive, unshaped block of ice. He appears curious and perhaps a bit puzzled, holding a small hammer and chisel, tools typically used for sculpting or chipping at ice. The setting is simple, with a plain yellow background that focuses attention on the man and his icy project. Then the man has begun to work on the ice. He's made some progress, as we can now discern the rough outline of a human form emerging from the block. The ice chips scattered around suggest he has been working diligently. His expression is one of concentration and determination, indicating his commitment to shaping the ice.
  
  In the right panel, the sculpture has taken a more defined shape, resembling a large hand giving a thumbs-up. The man, standing on a small ladder to reach the upper parts of the sculpture, looks thrilled with his work, as evidenced by his wide-open mouth, possibly cheering or laughing. This suggests a moment of triumph in his artistic endeavor. The ice sculpture, now recognizable as a large hand, has toppled over and is lying on the ground. The man is nowhere to be seen, presumably buried under the ice sculpture he worked so hard to create. This panel adds a layer of dark humor to the comic, as the man's creation, the symbol of success (thumbs-up), ironically leads to a comedic downfall.
  
  Overall, the comic strip uses visual storytelling to explore themes of creation, ambition, and unexpected consequences, all wrapped up in a light-hearted, humorous aesthetic.

description:
This comic strip illustrates a humorous scenario in two panels, playing on the theme of modern technology's impact on traditional practices.
  
  In the left panel, we see a group of four individuals gathered around what appears to be a hospital bed, looking solemnly at a figure lying on the bed. The setting suggests a serious, perhaps mournful, atmosphere typical of a hospital room where family or friends gather around a loved one.
  
  The right panel reveals a twist: the scene is not as somber as it first appears. The figure in the bed, who initially seemed to be a patient, is actually sitting up and actively participating in what is revealed to be a group activity. All individuals, including the one in the bed, are engrossed in their smartphones. Even the nurse, who is standing by the bed, is checking her phone. The bed and its occupant are not the focus of concern; instead, it seems to be a casual gathering where everyone is absorbed in their own digital world.
  
  This comic cleverly comments on how technology can sometimes overshadow traditional human interactions, even in settings where personal connection is expected to prevail. It uses the hospital scene, typically associated with care and attention to the sick, to highlight how pervasive and isolating technology can be.
caption:

  In the first panel, four individuals are seen from behind, gathered around a hospital bed. The focus is on their backs, and they appear to be looking towards someone lying in the bed, though the person in the bed is not visible from this angle. 
  
  In the second panel, the perspective shifts to show the scene from the side. It reveals that the individuals are not looking at the patient, but are instead engrossed in their smartphones. They are standing and sitting around the bed, oblivious to the patient. The patient, a man, is now visible and is sitting up in the bed, seemingly unnoticed by the visitors. He is wearing a hospital gown and a hat typically worn by patients. The nurse, who is also in the room, is standing at the foot of the bed, looking at a clipboard she is holding. She appears to be taking notes or reading something related to the patient's care.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the irony of modern communication methods where individuals are physically together yet emotionally distant. Despite being in the same room and engaged in an activity together, each person is absorbed in their own digital world, highlighting the isolation within connectivity facilitated by technology.
moral_mcq:

B. The comic illustrates the importance of staying aware and attentive to our surroundings when using technology.

description:
This comic image consists of two panels, each depicting different scenarios related to work efficiency and emotional responses over time.
  
  In the top panel, set against a warm orange background, a confident and smiling male character is shown seated at a desk. The text above him reads "我对工作是100%的投入" which translates to "I am 100% committed to my work." Behind him, a faint image of a serious-looking face suggests a dual personality or a hidden aspect of his character, hinting at the complexity of maintaining such high levels of dedication.
  
  The bottom panel, in contrast, has a cooler blue tone and shows a different scene that seems to represent the passage of time and its effect on the worker's efficiency and emotional state. The text lists percentages over the months: "Monday - 11%, Tuesday - 24%, Wednesday - 40%, Thursday - 23%, Friday - 2%." These percentages likely indicate the fluctuating levels of productivity or motivation throughout the weeks. Accompanying the text are three characters displaying varied emotional states ‚Äî stressed, tired, and extremely distressed ‚Äî which visually represent the decline in morale and energy as time progresses.
  
  Overall, the comic cleverly uses color and character expressions to contrast the initial enthusiastic commitment to work with the realistic, often challenging emotional journey through different times, highlighting the common workplace issue of burnout and fluctuating productivity.

The hamster now looks somewhat distressed or worried, with sweat droplets visible around its face, suggesting a sudden change in emotion or realization. The speech bubble reads, "我今天下班有空噢，晚上见~" which translates to "I am free after work today. Let's meet then" The background in this panel shows a silhouette of a cityscape, implying the setting may be urban or that time has passed since the first panel.

The hamster's change in expression humorously captures its regret when it realizes it actually does have free time, thus unintentionally committing to the plan.

description:

 The contradiction in this comic lies in the bear’s outward disappointment masking their inner satisfaction at the canceled plans.

description:
This comic consists of two panels, highlighting a humorous scenario:
 
 Top Panel: A person lies in bed, holding a phone and blushing intensely. The person looks embarrassed and exclaims in Chinese, "想女人了," which translates to "I’m thinking about women." Meanwhile, another figure in the background, holding a cup and looking puzzled, observes the scene with a question mark above their head.
 
 Bottom Panel: The focus shifts to the person in a contemplative state, still blushing, but this time thinking about food. A list of items is written in Chinese:
 
 "沪X阿姨" ("Shanghai Auntie"),
 "X阿婆" ("X Granny"),
 "X雪皇后" ("X Snow Queen"),
 "霸王X茶姬" ("King X Tea Princess"),
 "西X老太太" ("Western X Old Lady").
 These are humorous references to various popular food or drink brands with women-themed names. The background shows a milk tea cup, a plate of food, and desserts, suggesting that the person is actually craving snacks rather than women.
 
 The contradiction in this comic lies in the initial implication that the person is thinking romantically about women, only to reveal that their thoughts are actually focused on food brands associated with feminine names.

The text reads, "我在家里," which translates to "When I’m at home."
 
 Bottom Panel (Outside): The bear, now outside, looks timid and small, holding onto the sleeve of the person in front of it for comfort. Its posture and expression suggest nervousness or dependence. The text reads, "我在外面," which translates to "When I’m outside."
 
 The contradiction in this comic lies in the bear's starkly different behaviors: at home, it is confident, authoritative, and even smug, taking charge of the situation, while outside, it becomes shy, dependent, and anxious, clinging to someone for reassurance.

 The right panel (Chinese text: 「五分钟后」 meaning “Five minutes later”): The hamster stands at the checkout counter, arms overloaded with all sorts of groceries: bottles, snacks, rolls of toilet paper. A small caption near the hamster says 「好像没买酱油」, translating to “It seems I didn’t get the soy sauce.” The cashier looks on as the hamster struggles to juggle the pile of impulse purchases.
 
 The contradiction in this comic lies in the bear’s initial confidence that it can manage without a shopping cart for one simple item, contrasted with the chaotic reality of impulsively buying many items but forgetting the original purpose of the trip.

description:
This comic consists of two panels and is captioned with the words "YES," and "BUT" at the top of each respective panel, suggesting a contrast or contradiction between the two scenes.
 
 In the first panel, we see a dog sitting patiently at a pedestrian crossing, looking at a traffic light that is red, indicating that it is not safe to cross. The setting appears to be an urban street with a simple, muted color palette and minimal detail, focusing attention on the dog and the traffic light.
 
 The second panel shows a man crossing the street at the same pedestrian crossing where the dog is waiting. Despite the traffic light still showing red, indicating that it remains unsafe to cross, the man is in motion, stepping onto the crosswalk. This panel highlights the contrast in behavior between the obedient dog and the man who chooses to ignore the traffic signal.
 
 The comic comments on the theme of rules and obedience, contrasting the disciplined behavior of the dog with the rule-breaking action of the human. It playfully challenges the notion of "common sense" and who, between humans and animals, follows rules more strictly.
caption:
The comic consists of two panels, both set in an outdoor urban environment. Each panel features a traffic light post with a red light illuminated, and a zebra crossing on the road.
 
 In the first panel, a dog is sitting at the edge of the zebra crossing, facing the traffic light. The top of the panel has the word "YES," suggesting the dog is obeying the red light signal.
 
 In the second panel, the scene is almost identical, but now a man is depicted. He is crossing the street, ignoring the red light, and is in motion as indicated by the stride of his legs and the position of his arms. The word "BUT" appears at the top of this panel, contrasting with the dog's behavior in the first panel.
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the dog waiting obediently at the crosswalk despite the "walk" signal being on, while the human, despite understanding the signal, chooses to jaywalk. This highlights a humorous role reversal where the animal adheres to rules designed for human safety, whereas the human ignores them.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic suggests confidence in making risky choices, highlighting how unconventional decisions may defy norms, reflecting on personal priorities over collective safety considerations.

B. The comic illustrates how intelligence does not always translate to responsible behavior, emphasizing that actions often speak louder than status or reasoning.

C. The comic reflects animals’ instincts are comparable to human decisions, challenging typical views of intelligence, and revealing unpredicted wisdom.

D. The comic highlights flexible rule interpretations over strict adherence, suggesting human adaptability may compromise structured safety for perceived efficiency.

description:
This comic image humorously illustrates the contrasting states of a young woman before and after going out during the summer. The left panel is labeled "Going Out" and shows the woman looking cheerful and well-prepared for a sunny day. She is dressed in a casual summer outfit consisting of a yellow tank top and a blue skirt, and she is carrying a basket with flowers, suggesting a pleasant outing planned. Her expression is bright and optimistic, with large, sparkling eyes and a happy smile.
 
 The right panel, labeled "Coming Back," depicts the same woman, but now she appears exhausted and disheveled from the heat. Her hair sticks to her face, her tank top shows sweat stains, and her legs and face are covered in sweat drops. Her tongue is out, indicating her discomfort from the heat, and her eyes look tired. The flowers in the basket appear wilted, reflecting her own drained state.
 
 Overall, the comic captures the all-too-familiar experience of venturing out looking fresh and returning wilted by the summer heat, using exaggerated features and expressions to convey the humorous side of this common scenario.
caption:
The comic image is divided into two panels, both featuring the same girl depicted in different states labeled "Going Out" and "Coming Back." The title "SUMMERS" is written at the top center in pink.
 
 In the "Going Out" panel on the left, the girl appears cheerful and ready to go out. She has brown curly hair, wide eyes, and rosy cheeks. She is dressed in a sleeveless yellow top and a blue skirt. She is wearing blue socks with black shoes. The girl is holding a brown wicker basket with red flowers in it. Her posture is dynamic, suggesting movement and enthusiasm.
 
 In the "Coming Back" panel on the right, the girl looks exhausted and overheated. Her expression has changed to one of discomfort with her tongue sticking out and sweat droplets around her face and body. Her hair appears to stick to her face due to sweat. The yellow top now has a blue sweat stain around the waist, and her blue skirt remains the same. Her socks and shoes are the same as in the first panel. She is still holding the basket, which now appears empty and slightly tilted. The background in both panels is plain and light blue, focusing attention on the character.
contradiction: The contradiction in this comic illustrates the idealistic versus the realistic experiences of summer. On the left, the character is depicted as cheerful and neatly dressed with a basket of flowers, representing the hopeful, picturesque expectation of a summer outing; on the right, the same character appears exhausted, disheveled, and sweating, highlighting the often harsh and uncomfortable reality of summer heat when returning from an outing.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic suggests summer offers endless fun, portraying the joy of outdoor exploration despite heat, capturing an upbeat summer spirit.

B. The comic highlights how bright clothing affects mood, showing vibrant colors can boost energy and improve the summer vibe.

C. The comic illustrates the drastic change in appearance and comfort that one can experience during a summer day, highlighting the challenges of dealing with heat and humidity.

D. The comic implies the necessity of stylish accessories for outings, emphasizing their role in enhancing summer's charm and functionality.
title_mcq:
A. Winter Wind Woes 

B. Summer Sweat Struggle 

C. Autumn Leaf Labor 

D. Spring Breeze Battle
social_info:
1. **Summer Heat**: In many places, summer is associated with high temperatures that can cause discomfort and exhaustion after spending time outdoors.
 
 2. **Expectation vs. Reality**: People often start their day with enthusiasm and optimism, but the reality of harsh weather conditions can lead to unexpected fatigue and disarray.
 
 3. **Physical Effects of Heat**: Exposure to heat can lead to sweating, fatigue, and a disheveled appearance, which is humorously exaggerated in the comic.
 
 4. **Humor in Everyday Situations**: The comic uses exaggeration to humorously depict a common experience, making it relatable and amusing.
category: This comic belongs to the category of daily life humor, specifically focusing on weather-related experiences and personal discomfort during hot summer days.###Daily Life joke

In the first panel, a worried cow-like character asks their colleague, who is labeled “00后” ("Gen Z"), the question:
 “老板不给我涨薪怎么办？”
 ("What should I do if the boss doesn’t give me a raise?").
 
 In the second panel, the Gen Z colleague, still focused on their laptop, replies with an unconventional suggestion:
 “你可以通过减少工作量来给自己加薪”
 ("You can give yourself a raise by reducing your workload"). The cow looks confused and surprised at this unexpected advice, indicated by a question mark above its head.
 
 The contradiction in this comic lies in the stark contrast between the cow’s traditional expectation of earning a raise through negotiation or increased productivity and the Gen Z colleague’s modern, ironic suggestion to achieve the same outcome by reducing effort. The cow represents the conventional mindset of working harder to secure financial rewards, while the Gen Z colleague flips this logic on its head by prioritizing self-care and redefining what a "raise" means—less work for the same pay.

 In the second panel, the person is cooking something over an open fire, using pieces of the tree as fuel. The tree now lies on the ground, reduced to logs, while its stump is visibly present in the background.

 The contradiction in this comic lies in the stark contrast between harming someone and subsequently showing care and compassion toward them, creating a humorous yet ironic narrative.

description:
This comic contrasts the experiences of waiting for entertainment content in two different eras, labeled "BEFORE" and "NOW."
 
 In the "BEFORE" section, a young girl is depicted in a black-and-white setting, expressing her anticipation for the next episode of a television show, which she learns will only be released the following week. She appears resigned but patient, touching the screen of an old-fashioned, bulky television set. Her expression and posture reflect a mix of disappointment and acceptance as she realizes the wait involved.
 
 In the "NOW" section, the setting shifts to full color, showing a young woman lounging on a couch, surrounded by snacks. She is watching a modern, flat-screen TV and reacts with exaggerated shock and annoyance to a two-minute advertisement interrupting her viewing. Her dialogue bubble, "A 2-minute ad?! Why do I have to wait for so long?" highlights her impatience and the stark contrast in expectations for media consumption between the two eras.
 
 Overall, the comic illustrates how the evolution of media technology has significantly altered viewer expectations, with the modern audience having much less tolerance for waiting, even if it's just a short commercial break, compared to the more patient anticipation of weekly episodes in the past.
caption:

 In the "BEFORE" panel:
 The image depicts a young girl with short hair tied back with a bow, watching a bulky, old-style television. She appears engaged and slightly surprised, her hands pressed against the screen. The television shows a black and white image of what seems to be a knight and a horse. A speech bubble from the girl reads, "The next episode will only be released next week. We‚Äôll have to wait!"
 
 In the "NOW" panel:
 The scene shows a young woman with long blonde hair, wearing a red top, lying on a couch. She looks annoyed and is holding a modern, slim remote control while a bag of chips lies open beside her. The television screen is not visible, but it is implied that she is watching it. A speech bubble from her reads, "A 2-minute ad?! Why do I have to wait for so long?"
contradiction: The contradiction in the comic illustrates the change in expectations and patience over time when it comes to media consumption. While the older generation was accustomed to waiting a week for the next episode of a TV show, the younger generation in the comic is depicted as being impatient even with a brief two-minute advertisement.
moral_mcq:
A. The comic assumes rapid advancements in media have improved enjoyment but ignores how they might contribute to restlessness, contrasting with the benefits of less buffering in reality.

B. The comic illustrates the importance of patience and how it has diminished over time with the advent of instant gratification technology.

C. The comic suggests instant media provides relaxation benefits but overlooks how it can contribute to anxiety, contrasting with its portrayal of decreased waiting as stress-reducing.

D. The comic highlights impatience as a modern necessity, suggesting it benefits fast-paced lives, while ignoring the negative impact impatience can have in practical situations.
title_mcq:
A. Impulse Insatiable: Always Yearning
 

B. Waiting Woes: Then and Now
 

C. On-Demand Delay: Viewing Verge
 

D. Streamline Stops: Reluctant Recess

 2. **Viewer Expectations**: Recognizing the change in viewer expectations from patience with scheduled programming to impatience with even short interruptions.

This might suggest that while the men are indeed fit, their everyday appearance might not immediately reflect their physical capabilities, highlighting the difference between how people can appear in different contexts.

The comic image humorously contrasts two styles of jeans: high-rise and low-rise. It is divided into two panels, each featuring the same woman styled in different jeans.
 
 In the left panel, labeled "HIGH RISE JEANS," the woman is depicted wearing high-rise jeans that fit snugly around her waist, complemented by a tucked-in orange t-shirt. She appears confident and pleased with her appearance, as indicated by her posture and the admiring glance she gives herself. A thought bubble reads "What a sexy fit!" and small red hearts float near her, suggesting she feels attractive and stylish in these jeans.
 
 In the right panel, labeled "LOW RISE JEANS," the scene shifts to show the woman in low-rise jeans, which sit much lower on her hips. This time, her orange t-shirt hangs over the jeans. She looks back over her shoulder with a puzzled and slightly annoyed expression, questioning the practicality and fashionability of these jeans. A thought bubble contains her rhetorical question: "Why are these still made?" This panel humorously highlights the discomfort and impracticality often associated with low-rise jeans, contrasting sharply with the confidence and satisfaction expressed in the high-rise jeans panel.
 
 The contradiction in this comic lies in the stark difference in comfort, confidence, and appeal between high-rise jeans, which provide a flattering and empowering fit, and low-rise jeans, which cause discomfort and frustration, leading to questioning their relevance in modern fashion.

 The contradiction in this comic lies in the literal and illogical interpretation of sleep as a cause for tardiness, highlighting a humorous misunderstanding of priorities.
